display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

FindAllocationIndex used to scan every buffer allocation. Collective FFI handlers, such as Mosaic GPU kernels, call it for each buffer on every execution, in both the Prepare and Initialize stages. With thousands of allocations, this adds lookup overhead.

The first lookup builds a sorted index of non-empty allocations by start address in O(n log n). Later lookups binary search in O(log n) and check the single preceding entry. Identical duplicate allocations (same start address and size) return any matching index. Non-identical overlapping allocations are treated as an error: building the index logs an error and leaves the index empty so FindAllocationIndex returns std::nullopt.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove obsolete deviceless CUB scratch lookup tables

Now that CUDA CUB sort scratch sizing and kernel emission are computed purely in C++ from the target compute capability, the precomputed per-device `.textproto` lookup tables and `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` pass are no longer used on CUDA (and never contained entries for non-CUDA backends).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

display_title: [XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

ConditionalCodeMotion missed several soundness checks around roots and control dependencies:
1) Moving instructions with control dependencies across branch boundaries dropped their control edges (and failed RemoveInstruction on the original op), MoveInstructionOut unconditionally removed every existing GTE user of the conditional even if one had control dependencies, and ConvertSpecialMove unconditionally removed each branch root tuple even if it had internal users or control dependencies.
2) BoundariesToMoveInOrOut seeded move-out and move-user-in even when the conditional itself was the parent ROOT, allowing its output shape or root value to be mutated.
3) RestructureConditionalInstruction skipped redirecting pre-existing users of the conditional to new_tuple when the conditional was ROOT, leaving ConvertSpecialMove with duplicate GTEs at the same index.
4) WorthHoisting allowed non-tuple ROOT operands to be moved into branches, and MoveOperandIntoBranch deleted moved operands via user_count() == 0 instead of IsDead(), crashing when a ROOT operand or replicated ROOT broadcast lost its last user.

Reject instructions with control dependencies in WorthHoisting, broadcast replication, MoveInstructionOut user checks, and ConvertSpecialMove (including branch roots with internal users or control dependencies); skip seeding branch-out/user-in for a ROOT conditional; redirect all pre-existing users in RestructureConditionalInstruction regardless of whether the conditional is ROOT; and skip ROOT operands in WorthHoisting while guarding MoveOperandIntoBranch removal with IsDead().

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029038464

[XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

So this change adds `cub_sort_thunk_emitter` (split into `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_cuda` and `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_stub` behind `if_cuda_is_configured` on `deps`). display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB's host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds `cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB's `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables) and `cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: PR #53736: [XLA] Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

head_commit.message:
PR #53736: [XLA] Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53736

📝 Summary of Changes
`ComputeSpecialCaseCopies` can leave two entry-root outputs that are aliased to different parameters sharing one buffer. This fixes the bookkeeping so every repeat of the buffer except one gets copied.

🎯 Justification
When one value appears at several root indices, the loop that marks non-distinct indices records the first index for each buffer in `seen`. If a later index is aliased, it copies the earlier index, so the aliased output keeps the buffer. `seen` is never updated, though, so a third repeat copies the same earlier index again. For `tuple(x, x, x)` with {1} and {2} aliased to two parameters, only {0} is copied, and {1} and {2} still share a buffer, which merges the two donated parameters.

The GPU compiler reaches this after scheduling: `RunPostSchedulingCopyInsertion` removes the copies the schedule makes unnecessary, then relies on `AddSpecialCaseCopies` to keep the root buffers distinct. That is the cause of jax-ml/jax#39625, where a jitted function with donated state returns wrong values on GPU.

The fix sets `seen[buffer] = index` after the copy, so the next repeat is compared against the index that now holds the buffer. The two-repeat case behaves exactly as before. Copying the current index instead would also work, but it would change which output keeps the parameter buffer in the existing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
Three tests in `copy_insertion_test.cc` that call `AddSpecialCaseCopies` directly:
- one aliased and one unaliased repeat (existing behavior, unchanged)
- two repeats aliased to different parameters (existing behavior, unchanged)
- three repeats, two of them aliased: expects two copies and three distinct root buffers. On main this gets one copy, and {1} and {2} share a buffer.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None added. The end-to-end repro is in jax-ml/jax#39625. On GPU it only shows up when the schedule lets those copies be removed, which in my tests meant scalar or one-element outputs.

Copybara import of the project:

--

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points (`CubUniformSegmentedRadixSort{Keys,Pairs}Kernel`) with both primary and alternate radix bit-width policies across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Because XLA batched sorts have uniform segment sizes, each thread block computes its segment base offset directly from `blockIdx.x * segment_size`, avoiding the per-call H2D offset buffer copy while keeping each pass pure-Read/pure-Write for command buffers.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Compile XLA:CPU kernels as SmallPIC when emitting a .so

head_commit.message:
Compile XLA:CPU kernels as SmallPIC when emitting a .so

When using the new `xla_cpu_aot_emit_shared_object` flag, `CpuCompiler::RunBackend` will emit Position Independent Code (PIC) with the small code model (`SmallPIC`). Default behavior without the flag is unchanged.

To link kernels into a `.so`, we need PIC so `.text` has no absolute relocations, and the small code model for PC-relative addressing within 2 GiB.

Enabling SmallPIC on the `RunBackend` path also exposed two issues that weren't hit before (since it previously always used static/large-model code):

1. Unaccounted GOT size in `RuntimeDyld`: x86_64 PIC calls to external builtins emit `R_X86_64_PLT32`, and `RuntimeDyldELF` backs each stub with an 8-byte GOT entry in RW data without counting it in `relocationNeedsGot`/`computeGOTSize`. This overflows `ContiguousSectionMemoryManager`'s fixed RW block, so `EstimateUnaccountedGotSize` now computes an upper bound and reserves it upfront.
2. Missing `PIC Level` module flag on JIT modules: `CompileCpuExecutable` previously only set `pic_level`/`pie_level` on `AotLlvmMultipleModuleCompiler`, never on individual JIT modules. We now set those flags in `add_compiled_module` (skipping if already present, since `setPICLevel`/`setPIELevel` append rather than replace) so LLVM emits PIC codegen consistently on both paths.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove obsolete deviceless CUB scratch lookup tables

Now that CUDA CUB sort scratch sizing and kernel emission are computed purely in C++ from the target compute capability, the precomputed per-device `.textproto` lookup tables and `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` pass are no longer used on CUDA (and never contained entries for non-CUDA backends).

So this change deletes the lookup table infrastructure, generator targets, and `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize`, simplifies `SortRewriter` and `gpu_cub_sort_test` accordingly, and marks `xla_gpu_deviceless_cub_mode` as deprecated in `xla/xla.proto` while keeping the proto field and flag parser intact for backward compatibility with existing configs and AOT test fixtures.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

FindAllocationIndex used to scan every buffer allocation. Collective FFI handlers, such as Mosaic GPU kernels, call it for each buffer on every execution, in both the Prepare and Initialize stages. With thousands of allocations, this adds lookup overhead.

The first lookup builds a sorted index of non-empty allocations by start address in O(n log n). Later lookups binary search in O(log n) and check the single preceding entry. Identical duplicate allocations (same start address and size) return any matching index. Non-identical overlapping allocations are treated as an error: building the index logs an error and leaves the index empty so FindAllocationIndex returns std::nullopt.

display_title: [XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

ConditionalCodeMotion missed several soundness checks around roots and control dependencies:
1) Moving instructions with control dependencies across branch boundaries dropped their control edges (and failed RemoveInstruction on the original op), MoveInstructionOut unconditionally removed every existing GTE user of the conditional even if one had control dependencies, and ConvertSpecialMove unconditionally removed each branch root tuple even if it had internal users or control dependencies.
2) BoundariesToMoveInOrOut seeded move-out and move-user-in even when the conditional itself was the parent ROOT, allowing its output shape or root value to be mutated.
3) RestructureConditionalInstruction skipped redirecting pre-existing users of the conditional to new_tuple when the conditional was ROOT, leaving ConvertSpecialMove with duplicate GTEs at the same index.
4) WorthHoisting allowed non-tuple ROOT operands to be moved into branches, and MoveOperandIntoBranch deleted moved operands via user_count() == 0 instead of IsDead(), crashing when a ROOT operand or replicated ROOT broadcast lost its last user.

Reject instructions with control dependencies in WorthHoisting, broadcast replication, MoveInstructionOut user checks, and ConvertSpecialMove (including branch roots with internal users or control dependencies); skip seeding branch-out/user-in for a ROOT conditional; redirect all pre-existing users in RestructureConditionalInstruction regardless of whether the conditional is ROOT; and skip ROOT operands in WorthHoisting while guarding MoveOperandIntoBranch removal with IsDead().

head_commit.message:
PR #53736: [XLA] Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53736

📝 Summary of Changes
`ComputeSpecialCaseCopies` can leave two entry-root outputs that are aliased to different parameters sharing one buffer. This fixes the bookkeeping so every repeat of the buffer except one gets copied.

🎯 Justification
When one value appears at several root indices, the loop that marks non-distinct indices records the first index for each buffer in `seen`. If a later index is aliased, it copies the earlier index, so the aliased output keeps the buffer. `seen` is never updated, though, so a third repeat copies the same earlier index again. For `tuple(x, x, x)` with {1} and {2} aliased to two parameters, only {0} is copied, and {1} and {2} still share a buffer, which merges the two donated parameters.

The GPU compiler reaches this after scheduling: `RunPostSchedulingCopyInsertion` removes the copies the schedule makes unnecessary, then relies on `AddSpecialCaseCopies` to keep the root buffers distinct. That is the cause of jax-ml/jax#39625, where a jitted function with donated state returns wrong values on GPU.

The fix sets `seen[buffer] = index` after the copy, so the next repeat is compared against the index that now holds the buffer. The two-repeat case behaves exactly as before. Copying the current index instead would also work, but it would change which output keeps the parameter buffer in the existing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
Three tests in `copy_insertion_test.cc` that call `AddSpecialCaseCopies` directly:
- one aliased and one unaliased repeat (existing behavior, unchanged)
- two repeats aliased to different parameters (existing behavior, unchanged)
- three repeats, two of them aliased: expects two copies and three distinct root buffers. On main this gets one copy, and {1} and {2} share a buffer.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None added. The end-to-end repro is in jax-ml/jax#39625. On GPU it only shows up when the schedule lets those copies be removed, which in my tests meant scalar or one-element outputs.

display_title: [XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

ConditionalCodeMotion missed several soundness checks around roots and control dependencies:
1) Moving instructions with control dependencies across branch boundaries dropped their control edges (and failed RemoveInstruction on the original op), MoveInstructionOut unconditionally removed every existing GTE user of the conditional even if one had control dependencies, and ConvertSpecialMove unconditionally removed each branch root tuple even if it had internal users or control dependencies.
2) BoundariesToMoveInOrOut seeded move-out and move-user-in even when the conditional itself was the parent ROOT, allowing its output shape or root value to be mutated.
3) RestructureConditionalInstruction skipped redirecting pre-existing users of the conditional to new_tuple when the conditional was ROOT, leaving ConvertSpecialMove with duplicate GTEs at the same index.
4) WorthHoisting allowed non-tuple ROOT operands to be moved into branches, and MoveOperandIntoBranch deleted moved operands via user_count() == 0 instead of IsDead(), crashing when a ROOT operand or replicated ROOT broadcast lost its last user.

Reject instructions with control dependencies in WorthHoisting, broadcast replication, MoveInstructionOut user checks, and ConvertSpecialMove (including branch roots with internal users or control dependencies); skip seeding branch-out/user-in for a ROOT conditional; redirect all pre-existing users in RestructureConditionalInstruction regardless of whether the conditional is ROOT; and skip ROOT operands in WorthHoisting while guarding MoveOperandIntoBranch removal with IsDead().

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025895596

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB Onesweep radix sort kernels

Unbatched sorts larger than a single thread-block tile need a multi-block GPU sort algorithm to avoid falling back to slower sorting paths or linking CUB's runtime host dispatcher.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points for CUB's multi-portion Onesweep radix sort across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types: the value-independent histogram kernel (compiled once per key type in the keys-only shards and reused by pair shards), an out-of-place exclusive-sum kernel (`cub_sort_kernels_exclusive_sum.cu.cc`) that also zeroes per-(portion, pass) dynamic tile counters, and the Onesweep scatter kernels. `GetCubSortOnesweepKernelSpecs` extracts the single-architecture CUBINs together with statically parsed histogram register/shared-memory attributes for compile-time occupancy planning.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points (`CubUniformSegmentedRadixSort{Keys,Pairs}Kernel`) with both primary and alternate radix bit-width policies across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Because XLA batched sorts have uniform segment sizes, each thread block computes its segment base offset directly from `blockIdx.x * segment_size`, avoiding the per-call H2D offset buffer copy while keeping each pass pure-Read/pure-Write for command buffers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

Currently XLA executes CUDA CUB sorts via FFI custom calls to `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, which ties the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and prevents embedding sort kernels in AOT artifacts.

So this change adds the sharded `embeddable_cuda_library(..., register_with_cudart = False)` kernel infrastructure under `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/` together with the unified single-tile radix sort kernels (covering both unbatched and batched segments that fit in a single thread block) across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Each device `XlaChainedPolicy` is built from `cub_sort_policy.h` and checked with `static_assert`s so host planning and compiled single-architecture CUBINs stay in lockstep across CCCL versions.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

So this change adds `cub_sort_thunk_emitter` (split into `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_cuda` and `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_stub` behind `if_cuda_is_configured` on `deps`). The CUDA emitter computes Onesweep histogram occupancy statically from `DeviceDescription` and CUBIN ELF attributes via `cuda_occupancy.h`, packs kernel arguments via `KernelArgsPackingSpec`, and emits a flat `ThunkSequence` of `CustomKernelThunk`s (or `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk`s for single-element segments) with strict pure-Read/pure-Write `BufferUse` slices for `CommandBufferThunk` capture and update.

display_title: [XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

A JAX user jitting `jnp.concatenate([a[i], a[i+1:i+2]])` on CPU gets `[6. 6.]`
instead of `[5. 6.]` (jaxlib 0.7.1 through 0.12.1; correct with
`--xla_disable_hlo_passes=fusion`). Reported in
https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42758 and
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53472.

After optimization the gather becomes a dynamic-slice, so the fused concatenate
has two operands named `dynamic-slice.N` and `dynamic_slice.N`. The concatenate
emitter makes every concatenate operand its own subgraph. `PartitionedComputation`
names each subgraph `<computation>_<roots>` and passes it through
`llvm_ir::SanitizeFunctionName`, which turns both `-` and `.` into `_`. Both
operands end up with the same `func.func` name, so both call sites resolve to the
same function. With MLIR verification on this fails with
`redefinition of symbol named 'fused_computation_dynamic_slice_0'`. Without it,
both slots silently read the same operand.

The fix adds a `_<k>` suffix in the `PartitionedComputation` constructor when a
sanitized subgraph name is already taken. This matches the documented contract
of `Subgraph::name` ("A unique name of the subgraph. Used for function names.").
Names that do not collide are unchanged. The CPU and GPU emitters share this
code, so both get the fix.

Tests:
- `ComputationPartitionerTest.SubgraphNamesAreUniqueAfterSanitization`: checks
  that the two colliding roots get distinct names.
- `ConcatenateTest.FusedOperandsWithCollidingSanitizedNames`: end-to-end HLO
  execution test that expects `[5, 6]`. Without the fix it fails on CPU with the
  symbol redefinition error.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

FindAllocationIndex used to scan every buffer allocation. Collective FFI handlers, such as Mosaic GPU kernels, call it for each buffer on every execution, in both the Prepare and Initialize stages. With thousands of allocations, this adds lookup overhead.

The first lookup builds a sorted index of non-empty allocations by start address in O(n log n). Later lookups binary search in O(log n) and check the single preceding entry. Identical duplicate allocations (same start address and size) return any matching index. Non-identical overlapping allocations are treated as an error: building the index logs an error and leaves the index empty so FindAllocationIndex returns std::nullopt.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1027170366

display_title: [XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

`MeshProto::IotaTransform::transpose_perm` stores `int64` entries, but
`IotaTileAssignment::Create(dims, transform)` copied them directly into `int`
before validation. Out-of-range 64-bit values whose low 32 bits formed a valid
permutation (for example `[4294967297, 4294967296]`) were silently truncated
and accepted instead of rejected.

Add `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate(dims, const MeshProto::IotaTransform&)` to
range-check each 64-bit `transpose_perm` entry against `[0, perm_size)` before
narrowing to `int`, and delegate `Create(dims, transform)` to `TryCreate`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

FindAllocationIndex used to scan every buffer allocation. Collective FFI handlers, such as Mosaic GPU kernels, call it for each buffer on every execution, in both the Prepare and Initialize stages. With thousands of allocations, this adds lookup overhead.

The first lookup builds a sorted index of non-empty allocations by start address in O(n log n). Later lookups binary search in O(log n) and check the single preceding entry. Identical duplicate allocations (same start address and size) return any matching index. Non-identical overlapping allocations are treated as an error: building the index logs an error and leaves the index empty so FindAllocationIndex returns std::nullopt.

[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB's host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

Unbatched sorts larger than a single thread-block tile need a multi-block GPU sort algorithm to avoid falling back to slower sorting paths or linking CUB's runtime host dispatcher.

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

display_title: PR #53736: [XLA] Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

head_commit.message:
PR #53736: [XLA] Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53736

📝 Summary of Changes
`ComputeSpecialCaseCopies` can leave two entry-root outputs that are aliased to different parameters sharing one buffer. This fixes the bookkeeping so every repeat of the buffer except one gets copied.

🎯 Justification
When one value appears at several root indices, the loop that marks non-distinct indices records the first index for each buffer in `seen`. If a later index is aliased, it copies the earlier index, so the aliased output keeps the buffer. `seen` is never updated, though, so a third repeat copies the same earlier index again. For `tuple(x, x, x)` with {1} and {2} aliased to two parameters, only {0} is copied, and {1} and {2} still share a buffer, which merges the two donated parameters.

The GPU compiler reaches this after scheduling: `RunPostSchedulingCopyInsertion` removes the copies the schedule makes unnecessary, then relies on `AddSpecialCaseCopies` to keep the root buffers distinct. That is the cause of jax-ml/jax#39625, where a jitted function with donated state returns wrong values on GPU.

The fix sets `seen[buffer] = index` after the copy, so the next repeat is compared against the index that now holds the buffer. The two-repeat case behaves exactly as before. Copying the current index instead would also work, but it would change which output keeps the parameter buffer in the existing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
Three tests in `copy_insertion_test.cc` that call `AddSpecialCaseCopies` directly:
- one aliased and one unaliased repeat (existing behavior, unchanged)
- two repeats aliased to different parameters (existing behavior, unchanged)
- three repeats, two of them aliased: expects two copies and three distinct root buffers. On main this gets one copy, and {1} and {2} share a buffer.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None added. The end-to-end repro is in jax-ml/jax#39625. On GPU it only shows up when the schedule lets those copies be removed, which in my tests meant scalar or one-element outputs.

Fix special-case copies for a value repeated at several aliased outputs

buffer reaches an aliased output, but kept pointing `seen` at the first
index. A third repeat then copied the same index again and left two
outputs aliased to different parameters sharing one buffer. Point
`seen` at the index that now owns the buffer.

Now that CUDA CUB sort scratch sizing and kernel emission are computed purely in C++ from the target compute capability, the precomputed per-device `.textproto` lookup tables and `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` pass are no longer used on CUDA (and never contained entries for non-CUDA backends).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points (`CubUniformSegmentedRadixSort{Keys,Pairs}Kernel`) with both primary and alternate radix bit-width policies across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Because XLA batched sorts have uniform segment sizes, each thread block computes its segment base offset directly from `blockIdx.x * segment_size`, avoiding the per-call H2D offset buffer copy while keeping each pass pure-Read/pure-Write for command buffers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB Onesweep radix sort kernels

Unbatched sorts larger than a single thread-block tile need a multi-block GPU sort algorithm to avoid falling back to slower sorting paths or linking CUB's runtime host dispatcher.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points for CUB's multi-portion Onesweep radix sort across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types: the value-independent histogram kernel (compiled once per key type in the keys-only shards and reused by pair shards), an out-of-place exclusive-sum kernel (`cub_sort_kernels_exclusive_sum.cu.cc`) that also zeroes per-(portion, pass) dynamic tile counters, and the Onesweep scatter kernels. `GetCubSortOnesweepKernelSpecs` extracts the single-architecture CUBINs together with statically parsed histogram register/shared-memory attributes for compile-time occupancy planning.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Stage no per-arch ROCm run-time files in CPU-only test jobs

Tests in the ROCm CPU job run no GPU code but staged per-arch run-time files
(MIOpen CK libraries and databases, rocBLAS and hipBLASLt kernels, kpack
files), about 1 GB per test for gfx950, which pushed test inputs over the RBE
4 GB input limit.

TF_ROCM_RUNTIME_AMDGPU_TARGETS selects the architectures whose run-time files
are staged, independently of TF_ROCM_AMDGPU_TARGETS, which still selects what
device code is compiled for. It defaults to the same targets; "none" stages
none, which ci_rocm_cpu now uses.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

So this change adds `cub_sort_thunk_emitter` (split into `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_cuda` and `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_stub` behind `if_cuda_is_configured` on `deps`). The CUDA emitter computes Onesweep histogram occupancy statically from `DeviceDescription` and CUBIN ELF attributes via `cuda_occupancy.h`, packs kernel arguments via `KernelArgsPackingSpec`, and emits a flat `ThunkSequence` of `CustomKernelThunk`s (or `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk`s for single-element segments) with strict pure-Read/pure-Write `BufferUse` slices for `CommandBufferThunk` capture and update.

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

Enforcing element-type and per-shard-shape equality on `io_aliases` at IR verification missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style and layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality checks and instead requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, and matching effective memory kinds.

Physical per-shard byte-size compatibility depends on target-specific layout tiling and sub-byte packing, so it is deferred to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables, matching `ifrt.BitcastArrays`.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` and `ProgramMemoryTracer` to use the `IfrtCallOpInterface` alias helpers (`GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` and `getIoAliasPairs`), and adds `ProgramMemoryTracer` test coverage for aliased offloaded arrays and aliased arrays with differing dtypes, shapes, and layouts.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028983710

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Tile reductions of multi-reduce fusions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Tile reductions of multi-reduce fusions

Reduction dimension tiling was limited to fusions with a single reduction, and
the tiling search tried every power of two in [2, 256] as the reduction tile
size. This change allows us to tile fusions with more than 1 reduction as well.

Given that multi-reduce fusions can grow the tiling search space considerably, it is important to make sure we control this growth. Based on the microbenchmarks, it was sufficient to just include 1 tiled config (R/16), in addition to the untiled one, to cover most of the gains.

This change takes effect when we enable the tiling flag.

display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

Enforcing element-type and per-shard-shape equality on `io_aliases` at IR verification missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style and layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality checks and instead requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, and matching effective memory kinds.

Physical per-shard byte-size compatibility depends on target-specific layout tiling and sub-byte packing, so it is deferred to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables, matching `ifrt.BitcastArrays`.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` and `ProgramMemoryTracer` to use the `IfrtCallOpInterface` alias helpers (`GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` and `getIoAliasPairs`), and adds `ProgramMemoryTracer` test coverage for aliased offloaded arrays and aliased arrays with differing dtypes, shapes, and layouts.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Tile reductions of multi-reduce fusions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Tile reductions of multi-reduce fusions

Reduction dimension tiling was limited to fusions with a single reduction, and
the tiling search tried every power of two in [2, 256] as the reduction tile
size. This change allows us to tile fusions with more than 1 reduction as well.

Given that multi-reduce fusions can grow the tiling search space considerably, it is important to make sure we control this growth. Based on the microbenchmarks, it was sufficient to just include 1 tiled config (R/16), in addition to the untiled one, to cover most of the gains.

This change takes effect when we enable the tiling flag.

[ROCm] Stage each ROCm shared library once, under its SONAME

ROCm ships each shared library under several names (libMIOpen.so ->
libMIOpen.so.1 -> libMIOpen.so.1.0), and Bazel stages every name it is given

lists its other names. rocm_lib_glob() drops them from run-time data, and
rocm_lib_import() links against the unversioned name as a system-provided
interface library instead of staging it. Link-only globs (headers, the drm and
numa link inputs, toolchain_data) are unchanged.

display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: [TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.

head_commit.message:
[TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.
Previously, `DefineMoeNode` split MoE execution between host-side padded token bucketing (`[E, C, D]`) for multi-token prefill when `expert_indices` was a partition input and a weight-gather fallback for single-token decode or partition-internal `expert_indices`, which copied selected expert weights per token and prevented static `pack_b` and column-sum constant folding on blockwise-quantized weights.
- Unify `DefineMoeNode` in the TFLite YNNPACK delegate to lower `odml.moe_experts` ops (decode and prefill, symmetric `AffineQuantization`, `MultiAxisQuantization`, and `BlockwiseQuantization` in `int8` and `int4`) via `ynn_define_ragged_dot` and `ynn::define_blockwise_dot` over host-partitioned `[B * N * K, D]` expert slots and stationary 3D `[E, D_in, D_out]` weights.
- Trace partition-internal `RESHAPE` and `EXPAND_DIMS` views on `expert_indices` back to the external partition input (or constant) tensor, while rejecting MoE nodes whose `expert_indices` is produced by non-view partition ops.
- Flatten the MoE combine reduction from 4D `[B, N, K, D_out]` to 3D `[B * N, K, D_out]` followed by `ynn_define_split_dim` back to `[B, N, D_out]`, avoiding an outer loop over `B` and skipping YNNPACK subgraph rebuilds in `Prepare` when only sequence length `N` changes.
- Replace padded host token bucketing in `MoeDispatch`, `SetupMoeDispatch`, and `SetMoeDispatchShapes` with flat slot partitioning, removing `ShouldDispatchMoeOnHost`, `SetMoeDispatchData`, and `dispatch_moe_on_host`.

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. `Abort()` cancels a pending split wait, so it can't deadlock on the parent mutex. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the child-handle storage is intentionally left allocated, since NCCL may still write to it.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitAbortedCommunicatorsFails: splitting an aborted communicator fails with a clear error.

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

display_title: [XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

MoveUserInstructionsIn previously tried to predict whether tuple_use would become dead using only tuple_use->user_count() == 1, eagerly dropping its tuple slot and shifting later GTE indices before dead instructions were removed. That silently miscompiled when a sibling GTE read the same tuple_index, corrupted a live ROOT GTE before RunImpl crashed trying to remove it via user_count() == 0, and missed compacting multi-user GTEs whose consumers all moved in.

Always append moved-in results in MoveUserInstructionsIn while preserving existing slots, shardings, and OriginalValue entries in place, guard RunImpl removals with IsDead() and IsSafelyRemovable(), and compact unused branch outputs once in RemoveUnusedBranchOutputs from the actual surviving GTE users (updating tuple shardings and remapping kept OriginalValue subtrees via CopyOriginalValue).

display_title: PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

head_commit.message:
PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53709

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix copy insertion for stream-annotated computations on the parallel execution thread

🎯 Justification

computations annotated with _xla_stream_annotation (compute_on("gpu_stream:N")) run on the parallel execution thread. But RunPreSchedulingCopyInsertion still ran copy insertion only on main, so it skipped any while loop inside an annotated region. That loop never got the control edges or copies that copy insertion adds to keep in-place loop-carried updates safe.

As a result, the loop counter's in-place increment (i + 1) could be scheduled before the instructions that read i, and since buffer assignment gives i and i + 1 the same buffer, those readers saw the incremented value. A user's fori_loop with dynamic_slice/dynamic_update_slice on a second stream produced wrong results, with no error raised.

The fix runs the pre-scheduling copy-insertion pipeline on both the main and parallel threads.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:

🐛 Bug Fix

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

PR #52901: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52901

📝 Summary of Changes

- RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host disabled on ROCm.

🎯 Justification
Fix failing mgpu tests on ROCm by implementing missing functionality for LaunchReduce and CreateGpuAllocators and Skip tests for symmetric memory allocation (for now) and graph conditionals not supported by hipGrpah

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. `Abort()` cancels a pending split wait, so it can't deadlock on the parent mutex. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the child-handle storage is intentionally left allocated, since NCCL may still write to it.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitAbortedCommunicatorsFails: splitting an aborted communicator fails with a clear error.

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

ae55c49f8ea4faa8b3c67b7b4c1d714dc60d4fd0 by Jane Liu <janeliu@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

display_title: [XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

MoveUserInstructionsIn previously tried to predict whether tuple_use would become dead using only tuple_use->user_count() == 1, eagerly dropping its tuple slot and shifting later GTE indices before dead instructions were removed. That silently miscompiled when a sibling GTE read the same tuple_index, corrupted a live ROOT GTE before RunImpl crashed trying to remove it via user_count() == 0, and missed compacting multi-user GTEs whose consumers all moved in.

Always append moved-in results in MoveUserInstructionsIn while preserving existing slots, shardings, and OriginalValue entries in place, guard RunImpl removals with IsDead() and IsSafelyRemovable(), and compact unused branch outputs once in RemoveUnusedBranchOutputs from the actual surviving GTE users (updating tuple shardings and remapping kept OriginalValue subtrees via CopyOriginalValue).

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

head_commit.message:
PR #52901: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52901

📝 Summary of Changes

- RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host disabled on ROCm.

🎯 Justification
Fix failing mgpu tests on ROCm by implementing missing functionality for LaunchReduce and CreateGpuAllocators and Skip tests for symmetric memory allocation (for now) and graph conditionals not supported by hipGrpah

🚀 Kind of Contribution: 🧪 Tests

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

head_commit.message:
PR #46001: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 7th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001   <---- This PR
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions:
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting, Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported() ragged dispatch in the autotuner.
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

Please remove what does not apply:⚡️ Performance Improvement, ✨ New Feature

4f241b48219f4547a616e8cb24683224d970745a by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.
- Disables SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disables AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: [XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

HloSharding stores tuple shardings as a flat pre-order list of leaf shardings.
Previously, `HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` recursively parsed
`tuple_shardings` elements without rejecting nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` entries,
allowing nested tuple `HloSharding` objects that violated the flat-leaf
invariant (causing downstream `CHECK(!sharding.IsTuple())` aborts such as in
`GetSubSharding`) and permitting unbounded recursion on deeply nested protos.

Reject nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` elements before recursing in
`HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` with `InvalidArgumentError`, add a `DCHECK`
enforcing flat leaves in the private tuple constructor, guard
`ValidateNonTuple` against nested tuple elements, flatten tuple entry-argument
shardings (expanding unannotated tuple args by leaf count) in
`SetEntryTupleShardings` (and handle tuple shapes/shardings in
`RewriteLayoutWithShardedShape`), and clarify the `named_sharding` tuple
comments in `hlo_sharding.h` and `xla_data.proto`.

display_title: [XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

IotaTileAssignment::Transpose split reshape dims into prime factors by trial
division with a 32-bit counter. Large prime dims (e.g. from a deserialized
OpSharding) overflowed the counter and looped forever, and even a 64-bit counter
made trial division up to sqrt(2^62) a multi-second CPU cost. Zero-sized dims
also looped forever.

Transpose only needs the shortest common refinement of the tile dims and the
transposed reshape dims, which GetOrderedSubDims already computes in linear time
using divisibility checks. Use it instead, canonicalize zero-element iota tile
assignments in TryCreate, short-circuit Transpose for them, and make
ExtractCommonFactorSequence reject non-positive sizes instead of dividing by
zero.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028916517

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

A few-byte iota `OpSharding` can describe billions of devices. When its
replicated or subgroup dimensions do not align with the iota reshape
dimensions, `TryPartialTile` and `TrySubgroup` fall back to materializing an
explicit `Array<int64_t>`, so a tiny proto could allocate tens of GiB inside
`HloSharding::FromProto`.

`FromProto` now charges these iota-to-array fallbacks against a budget of 2^16
elements shared across all tuple elements, and returns InvalidArgument once it
is exceeded. Small non-aligned iota shardings still deserialize as before, and
the public `TryPartialTile`/`TrySubgroup` factories stay unlimited. `TrySubgroup`
now propagates `TryPartialTile` errors instead of CHECK-failing, and its
explicit-array fallback uses a single transpose instead of per-element index
vectors.

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.
- Disables SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disables AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: [XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

IotaTileAssignment::Transpose split reshape dims into prime factors by trial
division with a 32-bit counter. Large prime dims (e.g. from a deserialized
OpSharding) overflowed the counter and looped forever, and even a 64-bit counter
made trial division up to sqrt(2^62) a multi-second CPU cost. Zero-sized dims
also looped forever.

Transpose only needs the shortest common refinement of the tile dims and the
transposed reshape dims, which GetOrderedSubDims already computes in linear time
using divisibility checks. Use it instead, canonicalize zero-element iota tile
assignments in TryCreate, short-circuit Transpose for them, and make
ExtractCommonFactorSequence reject non-positive sizes instead of dividing by
zero.

display_title: [XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

`Array` computed its element count with an unchecked signed product, so
dimensions such as {3, 6148914691236517206} wrapped around to a small
allocation while the dimensions still described a huge array. A `MeshProto`
with such axis sizes and matching `device_ids` produced a `Mesh` whose later
transposes, indexing and tile iteration read and wrote out of bounds.

`Array` now CHECK-fails on negative dimensions and on overflow of the product
of its nonzero dimensions, both on construction and in `Reshape`. The
`Array(sizes, flattened_values)` constructor also checks the number of values
against the dimensions before allocating. `Mesh::FromProto` uses that
constructor for explicit device ids, so mismatched or overflowing meshes are
rejected without allocating the device id array.
