display_title: PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

head_commit.message:
PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53614

Fixes #53366.

When rewriting a value-only `sort -> slice` pattern (or lowering a value-only `topk` op), `TopkRewriter` produces a `"TopK"` custom call with a 2-parameter comparator. `TopKSplitter` splits that into a batched `"TopK"` custom call followed by a two-operand merge `sort` over `(values, indices)`, but reused `topk->to_apply()` unchanged. HLO verification rejects the merge sort because a two-operand sort requires a 4-parameter comparator:

```text
INTERNAL: during context [hlo verifier]:
Expected computation compare called from sort to have 4 parameters, has 2
```

When `topk->to_apply()` has 2 parameters, clone it with two trailing unused `s32[]` scalar parameters and attach the expanded 4-parameter comparator to both `batch_topk` and the merge `sort`. Updating `batch_topk` as well is necessary when `TopkSpecializer` does not specialize it (e.g. `k > 16`) and `TopkDecomposer` falls back to a two-operand `sort` because both tuple elements of `batch_topk` are read.

Added unit and GPU regression tests covering splitting a value-only `sort -> slice` rewrite, sharing one expanded comparator across multiple TopKs, and full GPU pipeline compilation of the `#53366` reproducer.

Tested on RTX 3080 (`sm_86`):
`bazel test --config=cuda --repo_env=HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_86 //xla/backends/gpu/transforms:topk_splitter_test_nvgpu_any` (11/11 pass).

head_commit.message:
PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53614

Fixes #53366.

When rewriting a value-only `sort -> slice` pattern (or lowering a value-only `topk` op), `TopkRewriter` produces a `"TopK"` custom call with a 2-parameter comparator. `TopKSplitter` splits that into a batched `"TopK"` custom call followed by a two-operand merge `sort` over `(values, indices)`, but reused `topk->to_apply()` unchanged. HLO verification rejects the merge sort because a two-operand sort requires a 4-parameter comparator:

```text
INTERNAL: during context [hlo verifier]:
Expected computation compare called from sort to have 4 parameters, has 2
```

When `topk->to_apply()` has 2 parameters, clone it with two trailing unused `s32[]` scalar parameters and attach the expanded 4-parameter comparator to both `batch_topk` and the merge `sort`. Updating `batch_topk` as well is necessary when `TopkSpecializer` does not specialize it (e.g. `k > 16`) and `TopkDecomposer` falls back to a two-operand `sort` because both tuple elements of `batch_topk` are read.

Added unit and GPU regression tests covering splitting a value-only `sort -> slice` rewrite, sharing one expanded comparator across multiple TopKs, and full GPU pipeline compilation of the `#53366` reproducer.

Tested on RTX 3080 (`sm_86`):
`bazel test --config=cuda --repo_env=HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_86 //xla/backends/gpu/transforms:topk_splitter_test_nvgpu_any` (11/11 pass).

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hide libnvJitLink leaks on failed create/link from leak checkers

`libnvJitLink` leaks memory on two failure paths, and `nvJitLinkDestroy` does not release it: `nvJitLinkCreate` rejecting the requested architecture (CUDA 13.2 and later) and `nvJitLinkComplete` failing to link (CUDA 13.1 and later). Tests that exercise these paths fail under leak checkers such as LeakSanitizer when built against those CUDA versions.

Wrap those two calls in `absl::LeakCheckDisabler`, gated on the `libnvJitLink` version reported at runtime, as `nvjitlink.cc` already does for the pre-13 `nvJitLinkAddData` leak.

display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target,
forcing XLA:CPU to pull in GPU dependencies. Our end goal is to replace the
unified `LowerTensorsPass` with separate CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes. As
the first step, separate the target-neutral core from the GPU patterns without
changing end-to-end CPU or GPU codegen.

Move the shared two-phase driver and target-neutral tensor and atomic patterns
into `lower_tensors_common` (`LowerTensors` and `LowerTensorsConfig`) with no
GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination buffers via
`mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and mark
`xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a
temporary thin wrapper that skips GPU patterns on CPU, and restrict `xla_gpu`
checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

The next step will add dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes in their
respective backend packages, migrate callers and tests, and remove
`LowerTensorsPass` from `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes`. That step
will drop the following GPU dependencies from XLA:CPU:
- `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns`
- `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect`
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_compute_capability`
- `//xla/stream_executor/rocm:rocm_compute_capability`

display_title: [XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

`Array` computed its element count with an unchecked signed product, so
dimensions such as {3, 6148914691236517206} wrapped around to a small
allocation while the dimensions still described a huge array. A `MeshProto`
with such axis sizes and matching `device_ids` produced a `Mesh` whose later
transposes, indexing and tile iteration read and wrote out of bounds.

`Array` now CHECK-fails on negative dimensions and on overflow of the product
of its nonzero dimensions, both on construction and in `Reshape`. The
`Array(sizes, flattened_values)` constructor also checks the number of values
against the dimensions before allocating. `Mesh::FromProto` uses that
constructor for explicit device ids, so mismatched or overflowing meshes are
rejected without allocating the device id array.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026360385

display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target,
forcing XLA:CPU to pull in GPU dependencies. Our end goal is to replace the
unified `LowerTensorsPass` with separate CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes. As
the first step, separate the target-neutral core from the GPU patterns without
changing end-to-end CPU or GPU codegen.

Move the shared two-phase driver and target-neutral tensor and atomic patterns
into `lower_tensors_common` (`LowerTensors` and `LowerTensorsConfig`) with no
GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination buffers via
`mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and mark
`xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a
temporary thin wrapper that skips GPU patterns on CPU, and restrict `xla_gpu`
checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

The next step will add dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes in their
respective backend packages, migrate callers and tests, and remove
`LowerTensorsPass` from `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes`. That step
will drop the following GPU dependencies from XLA:CPU:
- `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns`
- `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect`
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_compute_capability`
- `//xla/stream_executor/rocm:rocm_compute_capability`

display_title: PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

head_commit.message:
PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53614

Fixes #53366.

When rewriting a value-only `sort -> slice` pattern (or lowering a value-only `topk` op), `TopkRewriter` produces a `"TopK"` custom call with a 2-parameter comparator. `TopKSplitter` splits that into a batched `"TopK"` custom call followed by a two-operand merge `sort` over `(values, indices)`, but reused `topk->to_apply()` unchanged. HLO verification rejects the merge sort because a two-operand sort requires a 4-parameter comparator:

```text
INTERNAL: during context [hlo verifier]:
Expected computation compare called from sort to have 4 parameters, has 2
```

When `topk->to_apply()` has 2 parameters, clone it with two trailing unused `s32[]` scalar parameters and attach the expanded 4-parameter comparator to both `batch_topk` and the merge `sort`. Updating `batch_topk` as well is necessary when `TopkSpecializer` does not specialize it (e.g. `k > 16`) and `TopkDecomposer` falls back to a two-operand `sort` because both tuple elements of `batch_topk` are read.

Added unit and GPU regression tests covering splitting a value-only `sort -> slice` rewrite, sharing one expanded comparator across multiple TopKs, and full GPU pipeline compilation of the `#53366` reproducer.

Tested on RTX 3080 (`sm_86`):
`bazel test --config=cuda --repo_env=HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_86 //xla/backends/gpu/transforms:topk_splitter_test_nvgpu_any` (11/11 pass).

Merging this change closes #53614

display_title: [XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

HloSharding stores tuple shardings as a flat pre-order list of leaf shardings.
Previously, `HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` recursively parsed
`tuple_shardings` elements without rejecting nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` entries,
allowing nested tuple `HloSharding` objects that violated the flat-leaf
invariant (causing downstream `CHECK(!sharding.IsTuple())` aborts such as in
`GetSubSharding`) and permitting unbounded recursion on deeply nested protos.

Reject nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` elements before recursing in
`HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` with `InvalidArgumentError`, add a `DCHECK`
enforcing flat leaves in the private tuple constructor, guard
`ValidateNonTuple` against nested tuple elements, flatten tuple entry-argument
shardings (expanding unannotated tuple args by leaf count) in
`SetEntryTupleShardings` (and handle tuple shapes/shardings in
`RewriteLayoutWithShardedShape`), and clarify the `named_sharding` tuple
comments in `hlo_sharding.h` and `xla_data.proto`.

display_title: [XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

`Mesh::FromProto` and `AxisRef::FromProto` crashed with `CHECK` failures on
malformed protos. `Mesh::FromProto` also allocated the device array before
checking the number of device ids, so a tiny proto could request terabytes of
memory, and the product of mesh axis sizes could overflow `int64_t`.

Both now return `absl::StatusOr`. Add `Mesh::TryCreate` and
`IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate` for `MeshProto::IotaTransform`, validate
sub-axes with `AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis`, and check sizes, overflow and the
device id count before allocating. Callers that cannot yet propagate errors
unwrap the result.

head_commit.message:
Remove unused libdevice_path from xtile_compiler and TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass

`xtile_compiler` previously resolved the CUDA `libdevice.10.bc` path via
`nvptx::LibDevicePath` and threaded it into `TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass` as
the `libpath` attribute on `tt.extern_elementwise`. Nothing in MLIR, Triton, or
XLA reads this `libpath` attribute (`TranslateLLVMToLLVMIR` calls
`mlir::translateModuleToLLVMIR`, and actual libdevice linking happens later in
`nvptx::CompileToPtx` / `amdgpu_backend`).

Removes `GetLibdevicePath`, the `nvptx_libdevice_path` dependency from
`//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton:xtile_compiler`, and the unused
`libdevice_path` option on `TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass` (emitting
`libpath = ""`, matching `triton_xla_lower_atomics_pass` and
`triton_xla_lower_get_tid_pass`). This also decouples `xtile_compiler` from
`nvptx_libdevice_path` so `nvptx_*` / `cuda_root_path` can be tagged
`cuda-only`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Hide libnvJitLink leaks on failed create/link from leak checkers

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hide libnvJitLink leaks on failed create/link from leak checkers

`libnvJitLink` leaks memory on two failure paths, and `nvJitLinkDestroy` does not release it: `nvJitLinkCreate` rejecting the requested architecture (CUDA 13.2 and later) and `nvJitLinkComplete` failing to link (CUDA 13.1 and later). Tests that exercise these paths fail under leak checkers such as LeakSanitizer when built against those CUDA versions.

Wrap those two calls in `absl::LeakCheckDisabler`, gated on the `libnvJitLink` version reported at runtime, as `nvjitlink.cc` already does for the pre-13 `nvJitLinkAddData` leak.

display_title: [XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

`Array` computed its element count with an unchecked signed product, so
dimensions such as {3, 6148914691236517206} wrapped around to a small
allocation while the dimensions still described a huge array. A `MeshProto`
with such axis sizes and matching `device_ids` produced a `Mesh` whose later
transposes, indexing and tile iteration read and wrote out of bounds.

`Array` now CHECK-fails on negative dimensions and on overflow of the product
of its nonzero dimensions, both on construction and in `Reshape`. The
`Array(sizes, flattened_values)` constructor also checks the number of values
against the dimensions before allocating. `Mesh::FromProto` uses that
constructor for explicit device ids, so mismatched or overflowing meshes are
rejected without allocating the device id array.

`libnvJitLink` leaks memory on two failure paths, and `nvJitLinkDestroy` does not release it: `nvJitLinkCreate` rejecting the requested architecture (CUDA 13.2 and later) and `nvJitLinkComplete` failing to link (CUDA 13.1 and later). Tests that exercise these paths fail under leak checkers such as LeakSanitizer when built against those CUDA versions.

Wrap those two calls in `absl::LeakCheckDisabler`, gated on the `libnvJitLink` version reported at runtime, as `nvjitlink.cc` already does for the pre-13 `nvJitLinkAddData` leak.

display_title: [XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

`Array` computed its element count with an unchecked signed product, so
dimensions such as {3, 6148914691236517206} wrapped around to a small
allocation while the dimensions still described a huge array. A `MeshProto`
with such axis sizes and matching `device_ids` produced a `Mesh` whose later
transposes, indexing and tile iteration read and wrote out of bounds.

`Array` now CHECK-fails on negative dimensions and on overflow of the product
of its nonzero dimensions, both on construction and in `Reshape`. The
`Array(sizes, flattened_values)` constructor also checks the number of values
against the dimensions before allocating. `Mesh::FromProto` uses that
constructor for explicit device ids, so mismatched or overflowing meshes are
rejected without allocating the device id array.

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

display_title: [XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

IotaTileAssignment::Transpose split reshape dims into prime factors by trial
division with a 32-bit counter. Large prime dims (e.g. from a deserialized
OpSharding) overflowed the counter and looped forever, and even a 64-bit counter
made trial division up to sqrt(2^62) a multi-second CPU cost. Zero-sized dims
also looped forever.

Transpose only needs the shortest common refinement of the tile dims and the
transposed reshape dims, which GetOrderedSubDims already computes in linear time
using divisibility checks. Use it instead, canonicalize zero-element iota tile
assignments in TryCreate, short-circuit Transpose for them, and make
ExtractCommonFactorSequence reject non-positive sizes instead of dividing by
zero.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026361040

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

In AcquireSymmetricMemory Promise::Set wakes Await() before the worker threads unwind and Promise objects detroyed.
Therefore worker threads could still hold extra shared_ptr<SymmetricMemory> copies after the helper returned. That caused flakiness in AcquireSymmetricMemoryCachesByAddress during use_count() check.

Switch AcquireSymmetricMemory to exec.Execute with an absl::BlockingCounter so each worker writes its result directly into the caller's vector.

Also check window destruction via `std::weak_ptr::expired()` after `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` and `bigger.clear()` instead of inspecting `use_count()`.

display_title: [XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

A few-byte iota `OpSharding` can describe billions of devices. When its
replicated or subgroup dimensions do not align with the iota reshape
dimensions, `TryPartialTile` and `TrySubgroup` fall back to materializing an
explicit `Array<int64_t>`, so a tiny proto could allocate tens of GiB inside
`HloSharding::FromProto`.

`FromProto` now charges these iota-to-array fallbacks against a budget of 2^16
elements shared across all tuple elements, and returns InvalidArgument once it
is exceeded. Small non-aligned iota shardings still deserialize as before, and
the public `TryPartialTile`/`TrySubgroup` factories stay unlimited. `TrySubgroup`
now propagates `TryPartialTile` errors instead of CHECK-failing, and its
explicit-array fallback uses a single transpose instead of per-element index
vectors.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026362957

display_title: [XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

`MeshProto::IotaTransform::transpose_perm` stores `int64` entries, but
`IotaTileAssignment::Create(dims, transform)` copied them directly into `int`
before validation. Out-of-range 64-bit values whose low 32 bits formed a valid
permutation (for example `[4294967297, 4294967296]`) were silently truncated
and accepted instead of rejected.

Add `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate(dims, const MeshProto::IotaTransform&)` to
range-check each 64-bit `transpose_perm` entry against `[0, perm_size)` before
narrowing to `int`, and delegate `Create(dims, transform)` to `TryCreate`.

Synthetic streaming kernels of 64–512 MiB average −11.5%.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

In AcquireSymmetricMemory Promise::Set wakes Await() before the worker threads unwind and Promise objects detroyed.
Therefore worker threads could still hold extra shared_ptr<SymmetricMemory> copies after the helper returned. That caused flakiness in AcquireSymmetricMemoryCachesByAddress during use_count() check.

Switch AcquireSymmetricMemory to exec.Execute with an absl::BlockingCounter so each worker writes its result directly into the caller's vector.

Also check window destruction via `std::weak_ptr::expired()` after `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` and `bigger.clear()` instead of inspecting `use_count()`.

display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target,
forcing XLA:CPU to pull in GPU dependencies. Our end goal is to replace the
unified `LowerTensorsPass` with separate CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes. As
the first step, separate the target-neutral core from the GPU patterns without
changing end-to-end CPU or GPU codegen.

Move the shared two-phase driver and target-neutral tensor and atomic patterns
into `lower_tensors_common` (`LowerTensors` and `LowerTensorsConfig`) with no
GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination buffers via
`mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and mark
`xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a
temporary thin wrapper that skips GPU patterns on CPU, and restrict `xla_gpu`
checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

The next step will add dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes in their
respective backend packages, migrate callers and tests, and remove
`LowerTensorsPass` from `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes`. That step
will drop the following GPU dependencies from XLA:CPU:
- `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns`
- `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect`
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_compute_capability`
- `//xla/stream_executor/rocm:rocm_compute_capability`

head_commit.message:
PR #52901: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52901

📝 Summary of Changes

- RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host disabled on ROCm.

🎯 Justification
Fix failing mgpu tests on ROCm by implementing missing functionality for LaunchReduce and CreateGpuAllocators and Skip tests for symmetric memory allocation (for now) and graph conditionals not supported by hipGrpah

🚀 Kind of Contribution: 🧪 Tests

display_title: PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

head_commit.message:
PR #53614: [XLA:GPU] Fix TopKSplitter comparator arity for value-only TopK

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53614

Fixes #53366.

When rewriting a value-only `sort -> slice` pattern (or lowering a value-only `topk` op), `TopkRewriter` produces a `"TopK"` custom call with a 2-parameter comparator. `TopKSplitter` splits that into a batched `"TopK"` custom call followed by a two-operand merge `sort` over `(values, indices)`, but reused `topk->to_apply()` unchanged. HLO verification rejects the merge sort because a two-operand sort requires a 4-parameter comparator:

```text
INTERNAL: during context [hlo verifier]:
Expected computation compare called from sort to have 4 parameters, has 2
```

When `topk->to_apply()` has 2 parameters, clone it with two trailing unused `s32[]` scalar parameters and attach the expanded 4-parameter comparator to both `batch_topk` and the merge `sort`. Updating `batch_topk` as well is necessary when `TopkSpecializer` does not specialize it (e.g. `k > 16`) and `TopkDecomposer` falls back to a two-operand `sort` because both tuple elements of `batch_topk` are read.

Added unit and GPU regression tests covering splitting a value-only `sort -> slice` rewrite, sharing one expanded comparator across multiple TopKs, and full GPU pipeline compilation of the `#53366` reproducer.

Tested on RTX 3080 (`sm_86`):
`bazel test --config=cuda --repo_env=HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_86 //xla/backends/gpu/transforms:topk_splitter_test_nvgpu_any` (11/11 pass).

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target,
forcing XLA:CPU to pull in GPU dependencies. Our end goal is to replace the
unified `LowerTensorsPass` with separate CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes. As
the first step, separate the target-neutral core from the GPU patterns without
changing end-to-end CPU or GPU codegen.

Move the shared two-phase driver and target-neutral tensor and atomic patterns
into `lower_tensors_common` (`LowerTensors` and `LowerTensorsConfig`) with no
GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination buffers via
`mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and mark
`xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a
temporary thin wrapper that skips GPU patterns on CPU, and restrict `xla_gpu`
checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

The next step will add dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes in their
respective backend packages, migrate callers and tests, and remove
`LowerTensorsPass` from `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes`. That step
will drop the following GPU dependencies from XLA:CPU:
- `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns`
- `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect`
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_compute_capability`
- `//xla/stream_executor/rocm:rocm_compute_capability`

head_commit.message:
Remove unused libdevice_path from xtile_compiler and TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass

`xtile_compiler` previously resolved the CUDA `libdevice.10.bc` path via
`nvptx::LibDevicePath` and threaded it into `TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass` as
the `libpath` attribute on `tt.extern_elementwise`. Nothing in MLIR, Triton, or
XLA reads this `libpath` attribute (`TranslateLLVMToLLVMIR` calls
`mlir::translateModuleToLLVMIR`, and actual libdevice linking happens later in
`nvptx::CompileToPtx` / `amdgpu_backend`).

Removes `GetLibdevicePath`, the `nvptx_libdevice_path` dependency from
`//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton:xtile_compiler`, and the unused
`libdevice_path` option on `TritonXLAMathToLibdevicePass` (emitting
`libpath = ""`, matching `triton_xla_lower_atomics_pass` and
`triton_xla_lower_get_tid_pass`). This also decouples `xtile_compiler` from
`nvptx_libdevice_path` so `nvptx_*` / `cuda_root_path` can be tagged
`cuda-only`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

`ConcreteSharding` deferred checking shard-shape and index-domain counts to `Disassemble` and `IndexDomains`, and neither `ConcreteSharding` nor `ConcreteShardingSpec` verified that provided `index_domains` matched `shard_shapes`, matched the requested `shape` (including in `GetShardShape`), or lay within the logical `shape`.

Validate in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` that shard-shape counts match either all devices or addressable devices (short-circuiting before `AddressableDeviceList()` when matching all devices, and avoiding a duplicate `AddressableDeviceList()` lookup on error in `ConcreteShardingSpec::ToSharding`), and verify in `ConcreteSharding::WithDeviceAssignment` that addressable-only shardings preserve per-index device addressability. Update `ConcreteSharding::Disassemble` and `ConcreteSharding::IndexDomains` to support both all-shards and addressable-only representations consistently.

Validate eagerly in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` and `ConcreteShardingSpec::CreateIfValid` that `index_domains` (when present) matches `shard_shapes` in size and per-shard shapes and is contained within `shape`, and reject mismatched `shape` arguments in `IndexDomains` and `GetShardShape`. Update unit test fixtures in `array_impl_test_lib.cc` (which previously passed mixed shard-shape and index-domain counts) and tests whose `index_domains` extended past `Shape({30})`.

display_title: PR #46001: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

head_commit.message:
PR #46001: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 7th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001   <---- This PR
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions:
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting, Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported() ragged dispatch in the autotuner.
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

Please remove what does not apply:⚡️ Performance Improvement, ✨ New Feature

[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

Constructing a fresh `mlir::SymbolTableCollection` inside `IfrtCallLikeTrait::verifyTrait` rebuilt symbol tables for every `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` op, scaling quadratically with module size while duplicating lookups already performed in `verifySymbolUses`. In addition, external (bodyless) `func.func` callees were accepted by `CallOp` verification even though every IFRT IR import, compilation, and export pass requires defined callee bodies, forcing `CalleeSymbolManager` and downstream passes to duplicate null-callee and `callee.isExternal()` guards.

Move callee existence and `ifrt.function` exclusion into `IfrtCallLikeTrait::Impl::verifyCalleeSymbol`, invoked from `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses`. Reject external `func.func` callees in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`, and enforce via `HasParent<"::mlir::ModuleOp">` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses` that `ifrt.LoadedExecutable` ops sit directly in the enclosing `builtin.module`.

Drop the now-redundant null-callee and external-callee guards across `CalleeSymbolManager`, IFRT IR passes, and compilation/IR utilities, and update verifier and pass tests for the tightened contract (including replacing removed external-producer coverage with a multi-block producer test in `IfrtCopyConstantsPass`).

display_title: [IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

`ConcreteSharding` deferred checking shard-shape and index-domain counts to `Disassemble` and `IndexDomains`, and neither `ConcreteSharding` nor `ConcreteShardingSpec` verified that provided `index_domains` matched `shard_shapes`, matched the requested `shape` (including in `GetShardShape`), or lay within the logical `shape`.

Validate in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` and `ConcreteSharding::WithDeviceAssignment` that shard-shape counts match either all devices or addressable devices (short-circuiting before `AddressableDeviceList()` when matching all devices, and avoiding a duplicate `AddressableDeviceList()` lookup on error in `ConcreteShardingSpec::ToSharding`). Update `ConcreteSharding::Disassemble` and `ConcreteSharding::IndexDomains` to support both all-shards and addressable-only representations consistently.

Validate eagerly in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` and `ConcreteShardingSpec::CreateIfValid` that `index_domains` (when present) matches `shard_shapes` in size and per-shard shapes and is contained within `shape`, and reject mismatched `shape` arguments in `IndexDomains` and `GetShardShape`. Update unit test fixtures in `array_impl_test_lib.cc` (which previously passed mixed shard-shape and index-domain counts) and tests whose `index_domains` extended past `Shape({30})`.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

Enforcing element-type and per-shard-shape equality on `io_aliases` at IR verification missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style and layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality checks and instead requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, and matching effective memory kinds.

Physical per-shard byte-size compatibility depends on target-specific layout tiling and sub-byte packing, so it is deferred to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables, matching `ifrt.BitcastArrays`.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` and `ProgramMemoryTracer` to use the `IfrtCallOpInterface` alias helpers (`GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` and `getIoAliasPairs`), and adds `ProgramMemoryTracer` test coverage for aliased offloaded arrays and aliased arrays with differing dtypes, shapes, and layouts.

display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

display_title: [PJRT] Support partial tiled edge blocks in TransposePlan interleave and deinterleave kernels.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Support partial tiled edge blocks in TransposePlan interleave and deinterleave kernels.

For example, packing `s8[513, 512]` into `(8, 128)(4, 1)` interleaves groups
of 4 rows into 32-bit words. Rows `0..511` are 128 complete 4-row groups, and
row `512` is a trailing group with 1 valid row and 3 padding rows.

Previously, `TransposePlan` only used its vectorized interleave and
deinterleave kernels when the row count was an exact multiple of the inner tile
size `K`. A single incomplete trailing group caused the planner to reject those
kernels for the entire array, sending all full groups down a much slower
generic 2D transpose path (`99 µs` vs `15.5 µs` on `bf16[513, 512]`).

With this change, full `K`-row groups keep using the vectorized kernels
directly, and only the final incomplete group is handled specially:
- Interleave with `tile_padding` set: copy the valid rows and pad the missing
  rows in a small scratch buffer, then run the `K`-way interleave into the
  output (writing data and padding together).
- Interleave without `tile_padding`: write only the valid elements directly
  with a scalar 2D transpose so the unused padding slots in the output stay
  untouched.
- Deinterleave: unpack all `K` rows into a small scratch buffer and copy only
  the valid rows to the output.

Also documents the unset `tile_padding` contract in `transpose.h`. This brings
`513x512` `bf16` and `s8` multi-level pack/unpack back to the same speed as
`512x512` (2.9x to 6.4x faster), and adds partial-tile kernel-selection tests,
wide (> 512-column) edge-block tests, and multi-level `BM_Transpose` benchmark
cases.

[XLA:GPU] Skip token-typed heroes in DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2

`HasSupportedShapes` only rejected tuple-shaped operands and nested tuple results, so a hero with a `token[]` operand, a `token[]` result, or a `token[]` tuple result element was still wrapped into a dynamic slice fusion. Shardy's `mhlo.scan` partitioning previously hardcoded `i32` for the global and local scan index tensors and truncated the unpadded scan size via `static_cast<int32_t>`. display_title: [PJRT] Add per-chunk cache blocking and page-aware loop ordering to TransposePlan.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Add per-chunk cache blocking and page-aware loop ordering to TransposePlan.

Large transposes often walk tens of megabytes of memory along one axis before
returning to the next row, thrashing L2 cache — for example, transposing
`float[64, 224, 224, 3]` to `[224, 224, 3, 64]` walks 38 MiB of output per pass.

This change blocks long loops inside each chunk so the working set stays in L2
cache:
- Splits long outer loops into 256 KiB blocks (requiring at least a 4 KiB
  output-write burst per block so sequential writes aren't broken into tiny
  jumps) and re-orders the chunk's loops to interleave those blocks across
  dimensions. Any split whose halves remain adjacent collapses back into a
  single loop automatically.
- Adds a small 4 KiB page-stride penalty to loop ordering alongside the
  cache-line model so page-strided axes don't thrash the TLB.
- Sizes default 2D transpose blocks from the merged contiguous run lengths
  rather than pre-merge dimension sizes, now that cache blocking keeps the
  resulting larger blocks fast on Arm.
- Keeps partial-tile output padding strictly on hardware tile interiors so
  software-split loops never emit padding past the end of a chunk or buffer.
- Adds regression tests for cache-blocked padding and broadens the randomized
  test suite to cover shapes larger than 256 KiB, larger tiles, and exact tile
  multiples.

Across the full transpose benchmark suite, this reduces geomean CPU time by
2.2% to 5.3% across all five tested Arm and x86 CPUs, with 30% to 89% speedups
on large image-like and 3D transposes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029292092

display_title: [PJRT] Support multi-level tiling in TransposePlan.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Support multi-level tiling in TransposePlan.

Hardware layouts for narrow types use nested tiles — for example, `(8, 128)(2, 1)`
for 16-bit elements or `(8, 128)(4, 1)` for 8-bit elements — to pack adjacent
rows into 32-bit words. Previously `TransposePlan` only supported a single
tiling level, so callers had to run a separate repacking pass or emulate inner
tiles with manual dimension splits.

This change generalizes `TransposePlan` to arbitrary tiling depth:
- `Options::input_tiling` and `Options::output_tiling` now accept a list of
  tiling levels (`std::vector<Tiling>`, outermost to innermost, each dividing
  the enclosing level). The deprecated `Options::input_layout` field is removed.
- Loop construction, ordering, parallelization, chunk sizing, and partial-tile
  padding handle any number of tiling levels.
- Size-1 loops are dropped and adjacent contiguous loops are merged before
  picking the inner kernel, so kernel selection sees the real contiguous runs.
- Updates callers and adds unit and randomized tests for 2- and 3-level
  tilings, compact tiles, strided/broadcast inputs, and cache keys.

Performance on existing untiled and single-level tiled benchmarks is neutral
across Arm and x86 (geomean within 0.5% on all five tested CPUs).

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)

Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

Verified ABI version checks, default `BP(...)` vs. `fp6-in-8b` and rank-0 scalar tiling and padding, canonical memory-space layout validation, bit-plane reshape/slice bitcast checks, HLO layout/tiling passes, and literal linearizer round-trips in unit tests.

display_title: Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Add `BitPlaneProto` (`bit_planes` in `LayoutProto`, printed as `BP(w[:tiles])` or `BP(w@offset[:tiles])`) supporting both per-strip splits with outer `tiles` (such as `{1,0:T(256,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` and `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) and whole-tensor splits with empty outer `tiles` (such as 64-bit integer `{1,0:BP(32:(8,128))(32:(8,128))}`), while keeping `sizeof(xla::Layout)` unchanged. Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, `LayoutAssignment`, HLO simplifiers, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

Verified `BitPlaneProto` parsing, contiguous bit-plane validation, `LogicalBitWidth`, `ShapeUtil` and HLO pass preservation and guards, `CommonPjRtClient::CopyToMemorySpace`, `_hlo.pyi` stubgen, and Python `xc.Layout` round-trips in unit tests.

Donate PjRt-IFRT executable inputs according to donation intent.

`LoadedExecutable::GetDonatableInputIndices()` reports parameter donation intent (`jax.buffer_donor` and `tf.aliasing_output`), whereas XLA compilation may leave a donor unaliased when no compatible output buffer exists. head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on PJRT C API foreign callback invocations.

Callbacks, deleters, and vtable entries supplied across the PJRT C API by separately built shared libraries such as Python wheels lack Clang kCFI type hashes and trap with SIGILL under `-fsanitize=kcfi`.

This change annotates the plugin-side functions and local callable structs that invoke those foreign function pointers with `ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI`. Keeping each opt-out local preserves CFI checks on surrounding code, and using local callable structs instead of lambda attributes stays compatible with Abseil releases where the macro still expands to GNU `__attribute__`. Covers the PJRT C API wrapper, status utilities, chunk helpers, raw buffer and XLA transform internals, cross-host transfer extension, and custom partitioner callbacks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

When multiple threads hit `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` concurrently on the same device
during execution preparation, each thread independently triggers OOM recovery
(such as program eviction and memory defragmentation) and retries at the same
time. This causes redundant double-OOM recoveries and memory thrashing.

* Add per-addressable-device `DeviceOomState` and `OomSequencer` in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.h` and `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc`.
* Add `CommonPjRtClient::RunWithOomRetries`, which runs lock-free when the
  device is not under OOM, serializes recovery and retry attempts per device on
  `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and skips redundant recovery when another thread has
  already bumped the device OOM generation.
* Route `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::ExecutePrepareWithOomRetries` through
  `RunWithOomRetries`, resetting `launch_args` before waiting or recovering so
  partial buffer holds are released first.
* Add unit tests for `OomSequencer` concurrency, serialization, generation
  skipping, termination, and per-device independence in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client_test.cc`.

head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

The PJRT C API client invokes C function pointers supplied by dynamically loaded
plugins, including core API entry points, extensions, memory vtables, callbacks,
and deleters. Under kCFI, plugins built without matching instrumentation lack
CFI type hashes, causing indirect calls across the C ABI boundary to trap with
SIGILL.

call into loaded plugins, using small file-local helpers for calls inside
lambdas for compatibility with OSS Abseil releases pinned prior to the C++

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

PiperOrigin-RevId: 972771105

display_title: Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6.

head_commit.message:
Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

6-bit floating-point formats (`F6E3M2FN` and `F6E2M3FN`) previously defaulted to 8-bit `(4, 1)` container tiling in TPU device memory, wasting 25% of storage.

Assign `{1,0:T(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` (compact), `{1,0:T(T_0,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` (large 2nd minor and `kMatchDimension`), and 1D `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}` by default on TPU v5+ (keeping rank-0 `F6` scalars in 8-bit `{:T(512)}` tiling) while preserving explicit `T(T_0, 128)(4, 1)` `fp6-in-8b` layouts across XLA:TPU HLO transforms and PJRT. Teach TPU transfer-size, target layout, literal linearizer, and copy lowering utilities to size, pad, linearize, and DMA-transfer 3-sublane `(16, 128)` FP6 strips, and increment the TPU runtime ABI major version.

Verified ABI version checks, default `BP(...)` vs. `fp6-in-8b` and rank-0 scalar tiling and padding, canonical memory-space layout validation, bit-plane reshape/slice bitcast checks, HLO layout/tiling passes, and literal linearizer round-trips in unit tests.

head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

The PJRT C API client invokes C function pointers supplied by dynamically loaded
plugins, including core API entry points, extensions, memory vtables, callbacks,
and deleters. Under kCFI, plugins built without matching instrumentation lack
CFI type hashes, causing indirect calls across the C ABI boundary to trap with
SIGILL.

call into loaded plugins, using small file-local helpers for calls inside
lambdas for compatibility with OSS Abseil releases pinned prior to the C++
attribute migration, and add the corresponding core_headers dependency to
pjrt_c_api_multi_slice_config.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.sharding` region attributes, and `IfrtArrayType` allowed several inconsistent sharding and device-count configurations to pass `mlir::verify` (such as mismatched input/output device counts under unspecified sharding, `ifrt.sharding` device counts disagreeing with `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and arbitrary foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), forcing downstream verification passes to guard against them.

Tighten dialect and op verification to enforce these invariants upfront:

* Require `ifrt.CopyArrays` input and output arrays to have equal device counts even when sharding is unspecified, and drop the now-redundant mismatched-length bounds guards in `IfrtVerifyDonationPass`.
* Verify `ifrt.sharding` argument/result device counts against sibling `ifrt.devices` (or enclosing module `ifrt.num_devices` when `ifrt.devices` is absent).
* Restrict `IfrtArrayType` and `ifrt.sharding` to `IfrtShardingParamAttr` or `IfrtUnspecifiedShardingAttr` (rejecting foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), and delete the unused `kIfrtEntryFunctionAttrName` constant.

Update existing compilation pass tests whose `ifrt.sharding` attributes mismatched `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and add positive and negative unit and lit test coverage for the new checks.

display_title: Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Add `BitPlaneProto` (`bit_planes` in `LayoutProto`, printed as `BP(w[:tiles])` or `BP(w@offset[:tiles])`) supporting both per-strip splits with outer `tiles` (such as `{1,0:T(256,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` and `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) and whole-tensor splits with empty outer `tiles` (such as 64-bit integer `{1,0:BP(32:(8,128))(32:(8,128))}`), while keeping `sizeof(xla::Layout)` unchanged. Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, `LayoutAssignment`, HLO simplifiers, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

Verified `BitPlaneProto` parsing, contiguous bit-plane validation, `LogicalBitWidth`, `ShapeUtil` and HLO pass preservation and guards, `CommonPjRtClient::CopyToMemorySpace`, `_hlo.pyi` stubgen, and Python `xc.Layout` round-trips in unit tests.

Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

The PJRT C API client invokes C function pointers supplied by dynamically loaded

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.sharding` region attributes, and `IfrtArrayType` allowed several inconsistent sharding and device-count configurations to pass `mlir::verify` (such as mismatched input/output device counts under unspecified sharding, `ifrt.sharding` device counts disagreeing with `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and arbitrary foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), forcing downstream verification passes to guard against them.

Tighten dialect and op verification to enforce these invariants upfront:

* Require `ifrt.CopyArrays` input and output arrays to have equal device counts even when sharding is unspecified, and drop the now-redundant mismatched-length bounds guards in `IfrtVerifyDonationPass`.
* Verify `ifrt.sharding` argument/result device counts against sibling `ifrt.devices` (or enclosing module `ifrt.num_devices` when `ifrt.devices` is absent).
* Restrict `IfrtArrayType` and `ifrt.sharding` to `IfrtShardingParamAttr` or `IfrtUnspecifiedShardingAttr` (rejecting foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), and delete the unused `kIfrtEntryFunctionAttrName` constant.

Update existing compilation pass tests whose `ifrt.sharding` attributes mismatched `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and add positive and negative unit and lit test coverage for the new checks.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Remove redundant IFRT IR pass, lowering, and runtime checks

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Remove redundant IFRT IR pass, lowering, and runtime checks

Recent IFRT IR verifier and attribute tightening guaranteed stronger structural invariants across `ifrt.Call`, `ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.RemapArrays`, `IfrtDevicesAttr`, and `func.func` operations (including non-empty non-negative device lists, verified callee symbols and signatures, valid donation and remap bounds, and constrained `ifrt.module_type` values), leaving defensive guards, unreachable `CHECK`s, and dead error branches throughout downstream code.

Drop those already-redundant checks across import, compilation, program lowering, and runtime helpers. Remove the now-unused `CalleeSymbolManager::GetCallee` method in favor of direct `CallOp::getCalleeOp` lookups, simplify return types where failures can no longer occur (such as `ModuleTypeAnalysis::GetModuleType` and `GenerateLoadedExecutableOp`), and unify repeated `BitcastArraysOp` and `CopyArraysOp` validation onto `IfrtArrayOpInterface` alongside `GetMainFunction`. Also remove the unreachable `ifrt.reshard_function` fatal guard in `ProgramMemoryTracer` and stale TF-dialect documentation on `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass`.

This commit removes only checks already guaranteed by the current verifier.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

Callbacks, deleters, and vtable entries supplied across the PJRT C API by separately built shared libraries such as Python wheels lack Clang kCFI type hashes and trap with SIGILL under `-fsanitize=kcfi`.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Enforce two-tier callee nesting in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Enforce two-tier callee nesting in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`

Downstream IFRT IR passes only support `ifrt.Call` callees that are either flat functions in the enclosing `builtin.module` or outlined one level deep inside a named child `builtin.module`, yet `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` accepted arbitrarily nested symbol references and unnamed parents. That forced `CalleeSymbolManager`, `IfrtAtomProgramsToVhloPass`, and utility helpers to repeat depth, parent-type, and `sym_name` checks.

Enforce in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` that every `ifrt.Call` callee is a `func.func` directly inside either the enclosing `builtin.module` or a named direct child `builtin.module` (continuing to permit non-`@main` entry points in outlined modules). Remove the now-redundant nesting and `sym_name` checks from `CalleeSymbolManager`, `GetOutlinedAtomProgramModule`, `IfrtAtomProgramsToVhloPass`, `IfrtOutlineAtomProgramToModulePass`, and `IfrtCompileAtomProgramPass`, fixing the latent flat-`@main` misclassification in the outlining and compilation passes.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

head_commit.message:
Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

`GpuExecutable` now derives from the abstract `Executable` instead of
`HloModuleExecutable`. It keeps its optional `HloModule` and its `ModuleStats`
itself and implements `shared_module()`, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()`.

If the executable has the module, these return the module's values, exactly as
before. Without the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, or a `GpuExecutableProto`
without a serialized module), the executable answers from what it keeps:

- The input/output aliasing is rebuilt from the output info, which is already
  part of `GpuExecutableProto`.
- `module_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the new
  `GpuExecutable::Params::module_config` and `Params::buffer_donor_config`,
  which `GpuCompiler` fills from the module when it doesn't embed it.
  `module_config()` still CHECK-fails if neither is there, as today.

This way callers can get the metadata of an executable compiled with
`embed_hlo_module=false` through the `Executable` interface, and
`GpuExecutable` no longer needs `HloModuleExecutable`.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
new `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

All of this lives in `GpuExecutable`, `Executable` only sees the module through
the virtual accessors. The build-once state (mutex, factory, sticky error and
the built module) is in a separate heap-allocated struct, so executables
without a serialized module don't pay for it. Readers like `shared_module()`
don't take the lock. Until the module is built, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the
serialized module (the config with the same debug options the built module
gets) and from the output info, so asking for them doesn't build the module.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/backends/gpu/runtime:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the
concurrency test can also run with TSAN.

`//xla/tsl/lib/monitoring` is now also visible to `//xla/backends/gpu/runtime`,
which is where `GpuExecutable` lives, for the new counter.
