Disable CFI checks on PJRT C API boundary calls in `device_event`, `raw_buffer`, `pjrt_api`, and `inspect_sharding`.

Function pointers crossing the PJRT C API and dynamic plugin boundaries—including `dlsym`-loaded `GetPjrtApi`, plugin initialization, device event and promise vtables, raw buffer and external DMA vtables, and `InspectSharding` callbacks—may come from separately compiled shared libraries without Clang kCFI type hashes and trap with SIGILL under `-fsanitize=kcfi`.

display_title: Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

The PJRT C API client invokes C function pointers supplied by dynamically loaded
plugins, including core API entry points, extensions, memory vtables, callbacks,
and deleters. Under kCFI, plugins built without matching instrumentation lack
CFI type hashes, causing indirect calls across the C ABI boundary to trap with
SIGILL.

Apply ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI to the PJRT C API client functions that
call into loaded plugins, using small file-local helpers for calls inside
lambdas for compatibility with OSS Abseil releases pinned prior to the C++
attribute migration, and add the corresponding core_headers dependency to
pjrt_c_api_multi_slice_config.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

The PJRT plugin has its own copy of tsl::profiler::ProfilerLock. The
framework's ProfilerSession acquires the framework copy and then starts
the plugin profiler through the PLUGIN_Profiler C API, which never
acquired the plugin copy. Runtime code linked into the plugin, such as
CommandBufferThunk, therefore saw HasActiveSession() == false and kept
replaying command buffers as CUDA graphs under a profiling session, so
kernels were attributed to command_buffer_N instead of their HLO ops.

Acquire a ProfilerLock in PLUGIN_Profiler_Start (best effort: if the
lock is already held in this binary, HasActiveSession() is already true)
and release it in PLUGIN_Profiler_Stop or when the profiler is destroyed.

Fixes #50461

display_title: PR #52635: [XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

head_commit.message:
PR #52635: [XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52635

📝 Summary of Changes

The PJRT plugin (xla_cuda_plugin.so) is linked with its own copy of tsl::profiler::ProfilerLock. When the framework starts a profiling session, ProfilerSession takes the framework's copy of the lock and then starts the plugin profiler through the PLUGIN_Profiler C API. Nothing on the plugin side ever took the plugin's copy, so inside the plugin ProfilerLock::HasActiveSession() stayed false for the whole session.

CommandBufferThunk uses that check to fall back to op-by-op thunk execution while profiling (unless --xla_enable_command_buffers_during_profiling is set). With the plugin the fallback never happened: command buffers kept replaying as CUDA graphs and every kernel in the trace was attributed to hlo_op=command_buffer_N instead of its own fusion.

This change makes PLUGIN_Profiler_Start acquire a ProfilerLock and keep it in the PLUGIN_Profiler struct, and PLUGIN_Profiler_Stop release it. Destroying a started profiler releases it too (member destructor). The acquisition is best effort: if the lock is already held inside the plugin binary, HasActiveSession() is already true there, so Start just logs at VLOG(1) and continues as before. That keeps single-binary setups working (for example when this file is linked into the same binary as the ProfilerSession driving it; I believe libtpu also builds plugin_tracer_impl).

Two things for the import: plugin_tracer_impl now depends on @tsl//tsl/profiler/lib:profiler_lock, whose visibility is restricted internally (public in OSS), so it may need a visibility tweak; and the TPU plugin, if it shares this file, will now also acquire its own lock copy on Start.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50461. Anyone profiling JAX on GPU through the plugin (the normal pip install) currently gets no per-op device time for anything inside a command buffer, and the b/290773547 CUPTI + CUDA graph workaround is not in effect either. Verified end to end with a locally built plugin and jax 0.11.1: before, 180 of 180 graph-launched kernels in the trace were attributed to command_buffer_7/command_buffer_27 and the "Execute command buffer thunk as a regular thunk sequence" log line never appeared; after, the fallback triggers, 0 kernels come from CUDA graphs and each one carries its own HLO op name.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Three new tests in xla/backends/profiler/plugin/plugin_tracer_impl_test.cc, driving the real PLUGIN_Profiler_* functions through PluginTracer like the framework does:
- StartHoldsProfilerLockUntilStop: HasActiveSession() is false before Start, true after Start, false after Stop.
- DestroyReleasesProfilerLock: destroying a started PluginTracer releases the lock.
- StartWorksWhileAnotherSessionHoldsTheLock: with another ProfilerLock held, Start still succeeds, Stop does not release the other lock, and once it is released a new tracer acquires and releases the lock normally.
All three fail without the source change (HasActiveSession() stays false after Start).

🧪 Execution Tests:

No new execution test. Checked manually on one GPU (RTX 5070 Ti) with the issue's scenario: with the rebuilt pjrt_c_api_gpu_plugin.so loaded via PJRT_NAMES_AND_LIBRARY_PATHS, jax.profiler.trace now shows the command buffer fallback and per-op attribution.
Copybara import of the project:

display_title: [PJRT] Fuse output tile padding into BuildTransfer at the tile boundary.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Fuse output tile padding into BuildTransfer at the tile boundary.

Previously, `Planner::BuildChunkPlan` emitted output `tile_padding` fills as a
separate second pass (`BuildPadding`) over the entire chunk after
`BuildTransfer` finished. On arrays larger than L2/L3, this revisited cold
partial edge tiles after the transfer had already evicted them.

This change computes `pad_idx` in `ChunkPlanBuilder` as the first loop writing
inside a single output tile (`0 < ldb < tile_bytes`, or a 2D-kernel inner axis
stepped by `inc > 1`), and emits `BuildPadding(idx, partial)` immediately after
the transfer of `chunk_loops[idx..]` inside `BuildTransfer`:
- Outer batch and tile-exterior loops remain outside `pad_idx`, so each partial
  tile is padded while still hot in cache and full tiles run zero padding ops.
- All inner loops of the tile stay inside `BuildPadding`, preserving full
  `Fill1D` coalescing.
- Simplifies `Planner::BuildChunkPlan` to a single `builder.BuildTransfer(...)`
  call.
- Adds batched, transposed, and non-power-of-two output tile-padding unit tests
  and adds output tile-padded cases to `BenchmarkCases()` in `transpose_test.cc`.

head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on PJRT C API foreign callback invocations.

Callbacks, deleters, and vtable entries supplied across the PJRT C API by separately built shared libraries such as Python wheels lack Clang kCFI type hashes and trap with SIGILL under `-fsanitize=kcfi`.

This change annotates the plugin-side functions and local callable structs that invoke those foreign function pointers with `ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI`. Keeping each opt-out local preserves CFI checks on surrounding code, and using local callable structs instead of lambda attributes stays compatible with Abseil releases where the macro still expands to GNU `__attribute__`. Covers the PJRT C API wrapper, status utilities, chunk helpers, raw buffer and XLA transform internals, cross-host transfer extension, and custom partitioner callbacks.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

`ConcreteSharding` deferred checking shard-shape and index-domain counts to `Disassemble` and `IndexDomains`, and neither `ConcreteSharding` nor `ConcreteShardingSpec` verified that provided `index_domains` matched `shard_shapes`, matched the requested `shape` (including in `GetShardShape`), or lay within the logical `shape`.

Validate in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` that shard-shape counts match either all devices or addressable devices (short-circuiting before `AddressableDeviceList()` when matching all devices, and avoiding a duplicate `AddressableDeviceList()` lookup on error in `ConcreteShardingSpec::ToSharding`), and verify in `ConcreteSharding::WithDeviceAssignment` that addressable-only shardings preserve per-index device addressability. Update `ConcreteSharding::Disassemble` and `ConcreteSharding::IndexDomains` to support both all-shards and addressable-only representations consistently.

Validate eagerly in `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid` and `ConcreteShardingSpec::CreateIfValid` that `index_domains` (when present) matches `shard_shapes` in size and per-shard shapes and is contained within `shape`, and reject mismatched `shape` arguments in `IndexDomains` and `GetShardShape`. Update unit test fixtures in `array_impl_test_lib.cc` (which previously passed mixed shard-shape and index-domain counts) and tests whose `index_domains` extended past `Shape({30})`.

the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

6-bit floating-point formats (`F6E3M2FN` and `F6E2M3FN`) previously defaulted to 8-bit `(4, 1)` container tiling in TPU device memory, wasting 25% of storage.

Teach TPU transfer-size, target layout, literal linearizer, and copy lowering utilities to size, linearize, and DMA-transfer 3-sublane `(16, 128)` FP6 strips, and increment the TPU runtime ABI major version.

Verified ABI version checks, default `BP(...)` vs. `fp6-in-8b` and rank-0 scalar tiling, canonical memory-space layout validation, bit-plane reshape/slice bitcast checks, HLO layout/tiling passes, and literal linearizer round-trips in unit tests.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Add `BitPlaneProto` (`bit_planes` in `LayoutProto`, printed as `BP(w[:tiles])` or `BP(w@offset[:tiles])`) supporting both per-strip splits with outer `tiles` (such as `{1,0:T(256,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` and `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) and whole-tensor splits with empty outer `tiles` (such as 64-bit integer `{1,0:BP(32:(8,128))(32:(8,128))}`), while keeping `sizeof(xla::Layout)` unchanged. Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, `LayoutAssignment`, HLO simplifiers, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

Verified `BitPlaneProto` parsing, contiguous bit-plane validation, `LogicalBitWidth`, `ShapeUtil` and HLO pass preservation and guards, `CommonPjRtClient::CopyToMemorySpace`, `_hlo.pyi` stubgen, and Python `xc.Layout` round-trips in unit tests.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

## Status quo

`IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` links and inlines CppGen / YNNPACK bitcode intrinsics (`DefineIntrinsicFunctions` + `RunInlineAndOptPasses`), and then calls `llvm_ir::SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic(module)` across the entire module. That pass stamps LLVM's `contract` fast-math flag onto every `fadd`, `fsub`, and `fmul` in every function, including instructions that were just inlined from CppGen bitcode.

## Why

Adding `contract` to CppGen bitcode breaks error-free transformations such as `two_prod(a, b)` (`p = a * b; e = fma(a, b, -p);` followed by `n - p`). When both `fmul` and `fsub` carry `contract`, LLVM's `DAGCombiner` (especially on targets with aggressive FMA fusion such as AArch64) can fuse `n - (a * b)` into a single `fma(-a, b, n)` even when `p` has multiple uses. That skips the rounding of `p` while `e` still compensates for it, double-counting the rounding error.

CppGen bitcode libraries already emit explicit `@llvm.fma` or `@llvm.fmuladd` wherever FMA is wanted. Only XLA-emitted caller IR, polynomial approximations, and handwritten LLVM IR intrinsics rely on `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`.

## Design choices

- Add a function attribute `llvm_ir::kNoFpContractAttr` (`"xla_no_fp_contract"`) and make `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` skip functions that carry it.
- Tag CppGen bitcode definitions before `llvm::Linker::linkModules` in `CppGenIntrinsicLibrary::LinkIntoModule` (so colliding internal helpers renamed by the linker keep the attribute and pre-existing destination functions stay untouched) and in `GetCppGenFunction` (so `JitRunner` tests that load bitcode directly also skip contraction).
- Run `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` before `RunInlineAndOptPasses` in `IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` while keeping `SinkContractableFMulToFAddFSub` right after it (before sanitizer instrumentation). Because `AlwaysInlinerPass` does not copy unknown string attributes onto callers and `GlobalDCEPass` deletes the internal CppGen bodies, caller IR and handwritten IR intrinsics still get `contract` while inlined CppGen instructions keep `contract = false`.

## Compromises

- Post-inline cleanup passes (`InstCombine`, `EarlyCSE`) inside `RunInlineAndOptPasses` now see `contract` on caller instructions. The main `-O3` pipeline (including `Reassociate`) still runs before `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`. `EarlyCSE` intersects fast-math flags (`andIRFlags`), so CSE across a caller/callee boundary can only drop `contract` on a shared expression, never add it to a CppGen op. If a CppGen function returns a single-use `(-x) * y` into a contracted caller `fadd`/`fsub`, `InstCombine` could fold the sign across the boundary, which does not affect internal error-free transformations.
- Non-inlined `noinline` CppGen helpers retain the `"xla_no_fp_contract"` string attribute in final IR dumps.

## Alternatives

- **Emit `@llvm.fma` (or opt into `contract`) when emitting IR and delete `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`**: this is the intended long-term direction, so that contraction is explicit where code is generated and linked bitcode keeps IEEE rounding by default. Doing that today without regressing vectorization or changing `-O3` expression trees requires migrating XLA:CPU emitters and handwritten intrinsics off late module-wide contraction first.
- **Per-instruction metadata or fast-math flags during bitcode linking**: more invasive and fragile across LLVM passes than a function-level opt-out evaluated before inlining.
- **Work around inside each math library** (e.g., `fma(a, b, 0)` for `two_prod`): adds an extra FMA emulation penalty on targets without hardware FMA and forces every future CppGen math function to guard against unexpected backend contraction.

display_title: PR #52635: [XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

head_commit.message:
PR #52635: [XLA:GPU] Hold the profiler lock in the PJRT plugin while profiling

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52635

📝 Summary of Changes

The PJRT plugin (xla_cuda_plugin.so) is linked with its own copy of tsl::profiler::ProfilerLock. When the framework starts a profiling session, ProfilerSession takes the framework's copy of the lock and then starts the plugin profiler through the PLUGIN_Profiler C API. Nothing on the plugin side ever took the plugin's copy, so inside the plugin ProfilerLock::HasActiveSession() stayed false for the whole session.

CommandBufferThunk uses that check to fall back to op-by-op thunk execution while profiling (unless --xla_enable_command_buffers_during_profiling is set). With the plugin the fallback never happened: command buffers kept replaying as CUDA graphs and every kernel in the trace was attributed to hlo_op=command_buffer_N instead of its own fusion.

This change makes PLUGIN_Profiler_Start acquire a ProfilerLock and keep it in the PLUGIN_Profiler struct, and PLUGIN_Profiler_Stop release it. Destroying a started profiler releases it too (member destructor). The acquisition is best effort: if the lock is already held inside the plugin binary, HasActiveSession() is already true there, so Start just logs at VLOG(1) and continues as before. That keeps single-binary setups working (for example when this file is linked into the same binary as the ProfilerSession driving it; I believe libtpu also builds plugin_tracer_impl).

Two things for the import: plugin_tracer_impl now depends on @tsl//tsl/profiler/lib:profiler_lock, whose visibility is restricted internally (public in OSS), so it may need a visibility tweak; and the TPU plugin, if it shares this file, will now also acquire its own lock copy on Start.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50461. Anyone profiling JAX on GPU through the plugin (the normal pip install) currently gets no per-op device time for anything inside a command buffer, and the b/290773547 CUPTI + CUDA graph workaround is not in effect either. Verified end to end with a locally built plugin and jax 0.11.1: before, 180 of 180 graph-launched kernels in the trace were attributed to command_buffer_7/command_buffer_27 and the "Execute command buffer thunk as a regular thunk sequence" log line never appeared; after, the fallback triggers, 0 kernels come from CUDA graphs and each one carries its own HLO op name.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Three new tests in xla/backends/profiler/plugin/plugin_tracer_impl_test.cc, driving the real PLUGIN_Profiler_* functions through PluginTracer like the framework does:
- StartHoldsProfilerLockUntilStop: HasActiveSession() is false before Start, true after Start, false after Stop.
- DestroyReleasesProfilerLock: destroying a started PluginTracer releases the lock.
- StartWorksWhileAnotherSessionHoldsTheLock: with another ProfilerLock held, Start still succeeds, Stop does not release the other lock, and once it is released a new tracer acquires and releases the lock normally.
All three fail without the source change (HasActiveSession() stays false after Start).

🧪 Execution Tests:

No new execution test. Checked manually on one GPU (RTX 5070 Ti) with the issue's scenario: with the rebuilt pjrt_c_api_gpu_plugin.so loaded via PJRT_NAMES_AND_LIBRARY_PATHS, jax.profiler.trace now shows the command buffer fallback and per-op attribution.
Copybara import of the project:

--

[XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Dot rewriters that replace a dot with new instructions now derive the new dots
and the replacement via SetupDerivedInstruction, so they inherit the original
dot's metadata and frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This
covers DotAlgorithmRewriter (including the FP8xN decomposition in
hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc), ScaledDotRewriter, SplitkRewriter,
and GemmFusionSwapOperands. When ScaledDotRewriter computes the dot in a wider
type, the convert back to the scaled dot's type, which replaces it, is derived
from it too.

head_commit.message:
Wait for the allocation event in GPU AcquireExternalDmaAccess.

On GPU, newly allocated memory can still be used by an earlier computation until its allocation event finishes. Wait for that event in `StreamExecutorGpuRawClient::AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` before making the returned access available.

Also forward `GetDefinitionEvent()` and `MaterializeDefinitionEvent()` on `SlicedRawSEDeviceMemory` to its base buffer so slices wait too. This makes GPU and TPU behavior consistent. Once `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` becomes available, the memory is ready for external DMA.

head_commit.message:
Disable CFI checks on XLA PJRT C API client plugin calls

The PJRT C API client invokes C function pointers supplied by dynamically loaded
plugins, including core API entry points, extensions, memory vtables, callbacks,
and deleters. Under kCFI, plugins built without matching instrumentation lack
CFI type hashes, causing indirect calls across the C ABI boundary to trap with
SIGILL.

Apply ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI directly to the PJRT C API client functions
and lambdas that call into loaded plugins, and add the corresponding
core_headers dependency to pjrt_c_api_multi_slice_config.

Two things for the import: plugin_tracer_impl now depends on @tsl//tsl/profiler/lib:profiler_lock, whose visibility is restricted internally (public in OSS), so it may need a visibility tweak; and the TPU plugin, if it shares this file, will now also acquire its own lock copy on Start.

Fixes #50461. Anyone profiling JAX on GPU through the plugin (the normal pip install) currently gets no per-op device time for anything inside a command buffer, and the b/290773547 CUPTI + CUDA graph workaround is not in effect either. Verified end to end with a locally built plugin and jax 0.11.1: before, 180 of 180 graph-launched kernels in the trace were attributed to command_buffer_7/command_buffer_27 and the "Execute command buffer thunk as a regular thunk sequence" log line never appeared; after, the fallback triggers, 0 kernels come from CUDA graphs and each one carries its own HLO op name.

Three new tests in xla/backends/profiler/plugin/plugin_tracer_impl_test.cc, driving the real PLUGIN_Profiler_* functions through PluginTracer like the framework does:

- DestroyReleasesProfilerLock: destroying a started PluginTracer releases the lock.
- StartWorksWhileAnotherSessionHoldsTheLock: with another ProfilerLock held, Start still succeeds, Stop does not release the other lock, and once it is released a new tracer acquires and releases the lock normally.

No new execution test. Checked manually on one GPU (RTX 5070 Ti) with the issue's scenario: with the rebuilt pjrt_c_api_gpu_plugin.so loaded via PJRT_NAMES_AND_LIBRARY_PATHS, jax.profiler.trace now shows the command buffer fallback and per-op attribution.

The PJRT plugin has its own copy of tsl::profiler::ProfilerLock. The

display_title: Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

head_commit.message:
Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. `hlo_proto_` (with its mutex) is the last data member of
`Executable`, and all its producers and readers have moved away:

- Backends override the virtual `buffer_assignment_proto()` with state they
  own.
- HLO snapshots use the HLO that `Service` or `LocalExecutable` keep, or
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()`.
- `DumpingHloSnapshots()` replaces `dumping_snapshot()`.

So remove `set_hlo_proto()`, `hlo_proto()`, `dumping_snapshot()`, `hlo_proto_`
and its mutex. With that, `Executable` is an abstract base class without data
members, and `buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes pure virtual.
`HloModuleExecutable` returns nullptr, the backends that keep a buffer
assignment override it.

No behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that derive
from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable` instead
(or implement the pure virtuals).

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR `CopyArrays` and sharding verification

`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.sharding` region attributes, and `IfrtArrayType` allowed several inconsistent sharding and device-count configurations to pass `mlir::verify` (such as mismatched input/output device counts under unspecified sharding, `ifrt.sharding` device counts disagreeing with `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and arbitrary foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), forcing downstream verification passes to guard against them.

Tighten dialect and op verification to enforce these invariants upfront:

* Require `ifrt.CopyArrays` input and output arrays to have equal device counts even when sharding is unspecified, and drop the now-redundant mismatched-length bounds guards in `IfrtVerifyDonationPass`.
* Verify `ifrt.sharding` argument/result device counts against sibling `ifrt.devices` (or enclosing module `ifrt.num_devices` when `ifrt.devices` is absent).
* Restrict `IfrtArrayType` and `ifrt.sharding` to `IfrtShardingParamAttr` or `IfrtUnspecifiedShardingAttr` (rejecting foreign `IfrtShardingAttrInterface` implementations), and delete the unused `kIfrtEntryFunctionAttrName` constant.

Update existing compilation pass tests whose `ifrt.sharding` attributes mismatched `ifrt.devices` or `ifrt.num_devices`, and add positive and negative unit and lit test coverage for the new checks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

## Status quo

`IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` links and inlines CppGen / YNNPACK bitcode intrinsics (`DefineIntrinsicFunctions` + `RunInlineAndOptPasses`), and then calls `llvm_ir::SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic(module)` across the entire module. That pass stamps LLVM's `contract` fast-math flag onto every `fadd`, `fsub`, and `fmul` in every function, including instructions that were just inlined from CppGen bitcode.

## Why

Adding `contract` to CppGen bitcode breaks error-free transformations such as `two_prod(a, b)` (`p = a * b; e = fma(a, b, -p);` followed by `n - p`). When both `fmul` and `fsub` carry `contract`, LLVM's `DAGCombiner` (especially on targets with aggressive FMA fusion such as AArch64) can fuse `n - (a * b)` into a single `fma(-a, b, n)` even when `p` has multiple uses. That skips the rounding of `p` while `e` still compensates for it, double-counting the rounding error.

CppGen bitcode libraries already emit explicit `@llvm.fma` or `@llvm.fmuladd` wherever FMA is wanted. Only XLA-emitted caller IR, polynomial approximations, and handwritten LLVM IR intrinsics rely on `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`.

## Design choices

- Add a function attribute `llvm_ir::kNoFpContractAttr` (`"xla_no_fp_contract"`) and make `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` skip functions that carry it.
- Tag CppGen bitcode definitions before `llvm::Linker::linkModules` in `CppGenIntrinsicLibrary::LinkIntoModule` (so colliding internal helpers renamed by the linker keep the attribute and pre-existing destination functions stay untouched) and in `GetCppGenFunction` (so `JitRunner` tests that load bitcode directly also skip contraction).
- Run `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` before `RunInlineAndOptPasses` in `IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` while keeping `SinkContractableFMulToFAddFSub` right after it (before sanitizer instrumentation). Because `AlwaysInlinerPass` does not copy unknown string attributes onto callers and `GlobalDCEPass` deletes the internal CppGen bodies, caller IR and handwritten IR intrinsics still get `contract` while inlined CppGen instructions keep `contract = false`.

## Compromises

- Post-inline cleanup passes (`InstCombine`, `EarlyCSE`) inside `RunInlineAndOptPasses` now see `contract` on caller instructions. The main `-O3` pipeline (including `Reassociate`) still runs before `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`. `EarlyCSE` intersects fast-math flags (`andIRFlags`), so CSE across a caller/callee boundary can only drop `contract` on a shared expression, never add it to a CppGen op. If a CppGen function returns a single-use `(-x) * y` into a contracted caller `fadd`/`fsub`, `InstCombine` could fold the sign across the boundary, which does not affect internal error-free transformations.
- Non-inlined `noinline` CppGen helpers retain the `"xla_no_fp_contract"` string attribute in final IR dumps.

## Alternatives

- **Emit `@llvm.fma` (or opt into `contract`) when emitting IR and delete `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`**: this is the intended long-term direction, so that contraction is explicit where code is generated and linked bitcode keeps IEEE rounding by default. Doing that today without regressing vectorization or changing `-O3` expression trees requires migrating XLA:CPU emitters and handwritten intrinsics off late module-wide contraction first.
- **Per-instruction metadata or fast-math flags during bitcode linking**: more invasive and fragile across LLVM passes than a function-level opt-out evaluated before inlining.
- **Work around inside each math library** (e.g., `fma(a, b, 0)` for `two_prod`): adds an extra FMA emulation penalty on targets without hardware FMA and forces every future CppGen math function to guard against unexpected backend contraction.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Remove redundant IFRT IR pass, lowering, and runtime checks

Recent IFRT IR verifier and attribute tightening guaranteed stronger structural invariants across `ifrt.Call`, `ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.RemapArrays`, `IfrtDevicesAttr`, and `func.func` operations (including non-empty non-negative device lists, verified callee symbols and signatures, valid donation and remap bounds, and constrained `ifrt.module_type` values), leaving defensive guards, unreachable `CHECK`s, and dead error branches throughout downstream code.

Drop those already-redundant checks across import, compilation, program lowering, and runtime helpers. Remove the now-unused `CalleeSymbolManager::GetCallee` method in favor of direct `CallOp::getCalleeOp` lookups, simplify return types where failures can no longer occur (such as `ModuleTypeAnalysis::GetModuleType` and `GenerateLoadedExecutableOp`), and unify repeated `BitcastArraysOp` and `CopyArraysOp` validation onto `IfrtArrayOpInterface` alongside `GetMainFunction`. Also remove the unreachable `ifrt.reshard_function` fatal guard in `ProgramMemoryTracer` and stale TF-dialect documentation on `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass`.

This commit removes only checks already guaranteed by the current verifier.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and their cumulative non-zero product to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` or overflow `int64_t`), forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing domains that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and that the cumulative product of non-zero upper-bound dimensions (`origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]`) does not exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, validate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` and `operator+=` with `CHECK_OK` via a shared helper, route `IndexDomain::FromProto` through `IndexDomain::Create`, construct non-empty `Intersect` results via `UncheckedTag`, and drop redundant per-operand dimension-count checks in `Intersect` and `Contains`.

head_commit.message:
PR #53101: [ROCm] Non-temporal cache hints for gfx942

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53101

📝 Summary of Changes
On MI300, MLIR kernels mark large streamed loads and stores non-temporal. Loads need a buffer of at least 16×L2 (64 MiB) that is read once; stores need one qualifying output in a contiguous kernel.

🎯 Justification
Data touched once otherwise evicts reused data from L2 and from MI300X's Infinity Cache. This helps memory-bound fusions over large buffers.

Synthetic streaming kernels of 64–512 MiB average −11.5%.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Preserve constant weight tracking for YNNPACK pre-packing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Preserve constant weight tracking for YNNPACK pre-packing.

YNNPACK packs constant weight matrices into cache-friendly tiles once at initialization instead of re-packing them on every call. Previously, XLA only captured a `__ynn_fusion` input as constant when the direct operand carried `frontend_attributes={is_constant="true"}`. That check missed two common cases and forced constant weights to be re-packed dynamically on every execution:

* Literal `constant` instructions in frozen-weight graphs, which do not carry the `is_constant` attribute.
* Constant weights wrapped in zero-copy `bitcast` instructions inserted during layout assignment or reshape simplification.

Unwrap `bitcast` chains and mark constant `__ynn_fusion` operands with `is_constant="true"` during fusion creation and after post-layout passes so YNNPACK pre-packs them once.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Stop SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic from contracting CppGen bitcode.

## Status quo

`IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` links and inlines CppGen / YNNPACK bitcode intrinsics (`DefineIntrinsicFunctions` + `RunInlineAndOptPasses`), and then calls `llvm_ir::SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic(module)` across the entire module. That pass stamps LLVM's `contract` fast-math flag onto every `fadd`, `fsub`, and `fmul` in every function, including instructions that were just inlined from CppGen bitcode.

## Why

Adding `contract` to CppGen bitcode breaks error-free transformations such as `two_prod(a, b)` (`p = a * b; e = fma(a, b, -p);` followed by `n - p`). When both `fmul` and `fsub` carry `contract`, LLVM's `DAGCombiner` (especially on targets with aggressive FMA fusion such as AArch64) can fuse `n - (a * b)` into a single `fma(-a, b, n)` even when `p` has multiple uses. That skips the rounding of `p` while `e` still compensates for it, double-counting the rounding error.

CppGen bitcode libraries already emit explicit `@llvm.fma` or `@llvm.fmuladd` wherever FMA is wanted. Only XLA-emitted caller IR, polynomial approximations, and handwritten LLVM IR intrinsics rely on `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`.

## Design choices

- Add a function attribute `llvm_ir::kNoFpContractAttr` (`"xla_no_fp_contract"`) and make `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` skip functions that carry it.
- Tag CppGen bitcode definitions before `llvm::Linker::linkModules` in `CppGenIntrinsicLibrary::LinkIntoModule` (so colliding internal helpers renamed by the linker keep the attribute and pre-existing destination functions stay untouched) and in `GetCppGenFunction` (so `JitRunner` tests that load bitcode directly also skip contraction).
- Run `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic` before `RunInlineAndOptPasses` in `IrCompiler::RunIrPasses` while keeping `SinkContractableFMulToFAddFSub` right after it (before sanitizer instrumentation). Because `AlwaysInlinerPass` does not copy unknown string attributes onto callers and `GlobalDCEPass` deletes the internal CppGen bodies, caller IR and handwritten IR intrinsics still get `contract` while inlined CppGen instructions keep `contract = false`.

## Compromises

- Post-inline cleanup passes (`InstCombine`, `EarlyCSE`) inside `RunInlineAndOptPasses` now see `contract` on caller instructions. The main `-O3` pipeline (including `Reassociate`) still runs before `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`. `EarlyCSE` intersects fast-math flags (`andIRFlags`), so CSE across a caller/callee boundary can only drop `contract` on a shared expression, never add it to a CppGen op. If a CppGen function returns a single-use `(-x) * y` into a contracted caller `fadd`/`fsub`, `InstCombine` could fold the sign across the boundary, which does not affect internal error-free transformations.
- Non-inlined `noinline` CppGen helpers retain the `"xla_no_fp_contract"` string attribute in final IR dumps.

## Alternatives

- **Emit `@llvm.fma` (or opt into `contract`) when emitting IR and delete `SetAllowContractOnFpArithmetic`**: this is the intended long-term direction, so that contraction is explicit where code is generated and linked bitcode keeps IEEE rounding by default. Doing that today without regressing vectorization or changing `-O3` expression trees requires migrating XLA:CPU emitters and handwritten intrinsics off late module-wide contraction first.
- **Per-instruction metadata or fast-math flags during bitcode linking**: more invasive and fragile across LLVM passes than a function-level opt-out evaluated before inlining.
- **Work around inside each math library** (e.g., `fma(a, b, 0)` for `two_prod`): adds an extra FMA emulation penalty on targets without hardware FMA and forces every future CppGen math function to guard against unexpected backend contraction.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Propagate execution threads to region computations in HLO export.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Propagate execution threads to region computations in HLO export.

MLIR to HLO translation only set the execution thread of computations lowered
from functions with an execution_thread attribute. Computations lowered from
regions always ran on the main thread, even when nested in a function on another
thread. These include conditional branches, while bodies, fusions, and reducers.
An HLO to MLIR to HLO round trip thus moved them to the main thread. Passes that
run only on the main thread could then modify computations nested in a non-main
computation.

Computations lowered from regions now inherit the execution thread of the
function that contains them. Composite decompositions get the thread of their
decomposition function. Async-starts exported from stablehlo.async_start now run
on the thread of the enclosing function rather than the main thread. This
matches the thread of the computation they wrap. The reducer of an
all-reduce-start exported from mhlo.async_start runs on the thread of the
function that contains the mhlo.async_start, since that is where the
all-reduce-start is emitted, rather than on the thread of the async computation.
Nothing changes for functions on the main thread.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Remove redundant IFRT IR pass, lowering, and runtime checks

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Remove redundant IFRT IR pass, lowering, and runtime checks

Recent IFRT IR verifier and attribute tightening guaranteed stronger structural invariants across `ifrt.Call`, `ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.RemapArrays`, `IfrtDevicesAttr`, and `func.func` operations (including non-empty non-negative device lists, verified callee symbols and signatures, valid donation and remap bounds, and constrained `ifrt.module_type` values), leaving defensive guards, unreachable `CHECK`s, and dead error branches throughout downstream code.

Drop those already-redundant checks across import, compilation, program lowering, and runtime helpers. Remove the now-unused `CalleeSymbolManager::GetCallee` method in favor of direct `CallOp::getCalleeOp` lookups, simplify return types where failures can no longer occur (such as `ModuleTypeAnalysis::GetModuleType` and `GenerateLoadedExecutableOp`), and unify repeated `BitcastArraysOp` and `CopyArraysOp` validation onto `IfrtArrayOpInterface` alongside `GetMainFunction`. Also remove the unreachable `ifrt.reshard_function` fatal guard in `ProgramMemoryTracer` and stale TF-dialect documentation on `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass`.

This commit removes only checks already guaranteed by the current verifier.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and their cumulative non-zero product to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` or overflow `int64_t`), forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing domains that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and that the cumulative product of non-zero upper-bound dimensions (`origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]`) does not exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, validate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` and `operator+=` with `CHECK_OK` via a shared helper, route `IndexDomain::FromProto` through `IndexDomain::Create`, construct non-empty `Intersect` results via `UncheckedTag`, and drop redundant per-operand dimension-count checks in `Intersect` and `Contains`.

head_commit.message:

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data

caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as

display_title: Add external read and write entry points on PjRtBuffer and PjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Add external read and write entry points on PjRtBuffer and PjRtClient.

An external DMA engine (such as a NIC or a storage controller) reads and writes a buffer's device memory directly. It gets the address from `PjRtRawBuffer::AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`. The address alone is not enough. PJRT does not know about the transfer, so it does not order the transfer against its own work on the buffer, and `Delete()` or a donating `Execute()` does not wait for it. Today a caller can only set this up with methods that exist only on `CommonPjRtClient` and `CommonPjRtBuffer`. So add two entry points that do it for the caller:

- `PjRtBuffer::UseBuffer(cb)` is for reading an existing buffer. It takes a usage hold and calls `cb(raw, defined)`. `cb` starts the read after `defined` is ready, and returns a future that resolves when the read is done. Until then the memory stays alive, and `Delete()` or a donating `Execute()` waits.
- `PjRtClient::CreateBufferFromExternalWrite(shape, memory_space, cb)` is for writing a new buffer. It allocates the memory and calls `cb(raw, allocated)`. `cb` starts the write after `allocated` is ready, and returns a future that resolves when the write is done. This future defines the returned buffer, so consumers wait for it, and an error poisons the buffer. The memory stays alive until the write is done, even if the buffer is deleted first.

The write must wait for `allocated` because newly allocated memory can still be in use by earlier device work. On GPU, memory is safe to use only after the compute stream has finished the work that was enqueued before the allocation.

`cb` runs before the entry point returns. Both entry points support array buffers only. If the buffer is an error buffer without memory, `UseBuffer()` returns the buffer's error and does not call `cb`. Both are implemented in `CommonPjRtClient`, and other clients return `Unimplemented`.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Enforce two-tier callee nesting in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Enforce two-tier callee nesting in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`

Downstream IFRT IR passes only support `ifrt.Call` callees that are either flat functions in the enclosing `builtin.module` or outlined one level deep inside a named child `builtin.module`, yet `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` accepted arbitrarily nested symbol references and unnamed parents. That forced `CalleeSymbolManager`, `IfrtAtomProgramsToVhloPass`, and utility helpers to repeat depth, parent-type, and `sym_name` checks.

Enforce in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` that every `ifrt.Call` callee is a `func.func` directly inside either the enclosing `builtin.module` or a named direct child `builtin.module` (continuing to permit non-`@main` entry points in outlined modules). Remove the now-redundant nesting and `sym_name` checks from `CalleeSymbolManager`, `GetOutlinedAtomProgramModule`, `IfrtAtomProgramsToVhloPass`, `IfrtOutlineAtomProgramToModulePass`, and `IfrtCompileAtomProgramPass`, fixing the latent flat-`@main` misclassification in the outlining and compilation passes.

display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

Now that CUDA CUB sort scratch sizing and kernel emission are computed purely in C++ from the target compute capability, the precomputed per-device `.textproto` lookup tables and `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` pass are no longer used on CUDA (and never contained entries for non-CUDA backends).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points (`CubUniformSegmentedRadixSort{Keys,Pairs}Kernel`) with both primary and alternate radix bit-width policies across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Because XLA batched sorts have uniform segment sizes, each thread block computes its segment base offset directly from `blockIdx.x * segment_size`, avoiding the per-call H2D offset buffer copy while keeping each pass pure-Read/pure-Write for command buffers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB's host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds `cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB's `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables) and `cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

Constructing a fresh `mlir::SymbolTableCollection` inside `IfrtCallLikeTrait::verifyTrait` rebuilt symbol tables for every `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` op, scaling quadratically with module size while duplicating lookups already performed in `verifySymbolUses`. In addition, external (bodyless) `func.func` callees were accepted by `CallOp` verification even though every IFRT IR import, compilation, and export pass requires defined callee bodies, forcing `CalleeSymbolManager` and downstream passes to duplicate null-callee and `callee.isExternal()` guards.

Move callee existence and `ifrt.function` exclusion into `IfrtCallLikeTrait::Impl::verifyCalleeSymbol`, invoked from `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses`. Reject external `func.func` callees in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`, and enforce via `HasParent<"::mlir::ModuleOp">` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses` that `ifrt.LoadedExecutable` ops sit directly in the enclosing `builtin.module`.

Drop the now-redundant null-callee and external-callee guards across `CalleeSymbolManager`, IFRT IR passes, and compilation/IR utilities, and update verifier and pass tests for the tightened contract (including replacing removed external-producer coverage with a multi-block producer test in `IfrtCopyConstantsPass`).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

A JAX user jitting `jnp.concatenate([a[i], a[i+1:i+2]])` on CPU gets `[6. 6.]`
instead of `[5. 6.]` (jaxlib 0.7.1 through 0.12.1; correct with
`--xla_disable_hlo_passes=fusion`). Reported in
https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42758 and
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53472.

After optimization the gather becomes a dynamic-slice, so the fused concatenate
has two operands named `dynamic-slice.N` and `dynamic_slice.N`. The concatenate
emitter makes every concatenate operand its own subgraph. `PartitionedComputation`
names each subgraph `<computation>_<roots>` and passes it through
`llvm_ir::SanitizeFunctionName`, which turns both `-` and `.` into `_`. Both
operands end up with the same `func.func` name, so both call sites resolve to the
same function. With MLIR verification on this fails with
`redefinition of symbol named 'fused_computation_dynamic_slice_0'`. Without it,
both slots silently read the same operand.

The fix adds a `_<k>` suffix in the `PartitionedComputation` constructor when a
sanitized subgraph name is already taken. This matches the documented contract
of `Subgraph::name` ("A unique name of the subgraph. Used for function names.").
Names that do not collide are unchanged. The CPU and GPU emitters share this
code, so both get the fix.

Tests:
- `ComputationPartitionerTest.SubgraphNamesAreUniqueAfterSanitization`: checks
  that the two colliding roots get distinct names.
- `ConcatenateTest.FusedOperandsWithCollidingSanitizedNames`: end-to-end HLO
  execution test that expects `[5, 6]`. Without the fix it fails on CPU with the
  symbol redefinition error.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB Onesweep radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB Onesweep radix sort kernels

Unbatched sorts larger than a single thread-block tile need a multi-block GPU sort algorithm to avoid falling back to slower sorting paths or linking CUB's runtime host dispatcher.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points for CUB's multi-portion Onesweep radix sort across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types: the value-independent histogram kernel (compiled once per key type in the keys-only shards and reused by pair shards), an out-of-place exclusive-sum kernel (`cub_sort_kernels_exclusive_sum.cu.cc`) that also zeroes per-(portion, pass) dynamic tile counters, and the Onesweep scatter kernels. `GetCubSortOnesweepKernelSpecs` extracts the single-architecture CUBINs together with statically parsed histogram register/shared-memory attributes for compile-time occupancy planning.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` callee verification in `verifySymbolUses`

Constructing a fresh `mlir::SymbolTableCollection` inside `IfrtCallLikeTrait::verifyTrait` rebuilt symbol tables for every `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` op, scaling quadratically with module size while duplicating lookups already performed in `verifySymbolUses`. In addition, external (bodyless) `func.func` callees were accepted by `CallOp` verification even though every IFRT IR import, compilation, and export pass requires defined callee bodies, forcing `CalleeSymbolManager` and downstream passes to duplicate null-callee and `callee.isExternal()` guards.

Move callee existence and `ifrt.function` exclusion into `IfrtCallLikeTrait::Impl::verifyCalleeSymbol`, invoked from `CallOp::verifySymbolUses` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses`. Reject external `func.func` callees in `CallOp::verifySymbolUses`, and enforce via `HasParent<"::mlir::ModuleOp">` and `CallLoadedExecutableOp::verifySymbolUses` that `ifrt.LoadedExecutable` ops sit directly in the enclosing `builtin.module`.

Drop the now-redundant null-callee and external-callee guards across `CalleeSymbolManager`, IFRT IR passes, and compilation/IR utilities, and update verifier and pass tests for the tightened contract (including replacing removed external-producer coverage with a multi-block producer test in `IfrtCopyConstantsPass`).

display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and emitter into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` on CUDA directly to embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences (and `DeviceToDeviceCopyThunk` for single-element segments).

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Compile XLA:CPU kernels as SmallPIC when emitting a .so

head_commit.message:
Compile XLA:CPU kernels as SmallPIC when emitting a .so

When using the new `xla_cpu_aot_emit_shared_object` flag, `CpuCompiler::RunBackend` will emit Position Independent Code (PIC) with the small code model (`SmallPIC`). Default behavior without the flag is unchanged.

To link kernels into a `.so`, we need PIC so `.text` has no absolute relocations, and the small code model for PC-relative addressing within 2 GiB.

Enabling SmallPIC on the `RunBackend` path also exposed two issues that weren't hit before (since it previously always used static/large-model code):

1. Unaccounted GOT size in `RuntimeDyld`: x86_64 PIC calls to external builtins emit `R_X86_64_PLT32`, and `RuntimeDyldELF` backs each stub with an 8-byte GOT entry in RW data without counting it in `relocationNeedsGot`/`computeGOTSize`. This overflows `ContiguousSectionMemoryManager`'s fixed RW block, so `EstimateUnaccountedGotSize` now computes an upper bound and reserves it upfront.
2. Missing `PIC Level` module flag on JIT modules: `CompileCpuExecutable` previously only set `pic_level`/`pie_level` on `AotLlvmMultipleModuleCompiler`, never on individual JIT modules. We now set those flags in `add_compiled_module` (skipping if already present, since `setPICLevel`/`setPIELevel` append rather than replace) so LLVM emits PIC codegen consistently on both paths.

JAX `emit_python_callback` lowerings from `sparse.linalg.spsolve` or ordered
`debug.callback`). Only copy `mhlo.sharding` onto the new `get_tuple_element`
op when it is present.
